# FreezerTest knowledge base

Version: **0.3 — owner review and component photographs** · Updated: **29 October 2026**

This knowledge base explains the FreezerTest apparatus, control software, test sequence, data, and analysis methodology. It is intended for operators, colleagues, and a local AI answering questions about the test. It describes a particular source snapshot, not a certified operating procedure or a validated hardware inventory.

The original code review covered **33 shared Python/shell files**, identical to GitHub commit `df4ccebbbd0f41e32f5ae415e967728e5845d56b` (12 October 2026), plus the local configuration. Three project chats supplied historical context. Owner reviews on **27 and 29 October** add component identities, nine component photographs, six filter-wheel CAD files, the usual probe map, target/illumination details, and operating corrections. Those confirmations supersede conflicting historical assumptions. Unanswered questions remain in one [review register](09-review-questions-and-gaps.md). See [sources and maintenance](10-sources-and-maintenance.md) for provenance.

## Evidence labels

- **Implemented / source-derived:** visible behavior in the reviewed code. This does not prove the deployed camera has the same files.
- **Configured:** a value in the reviewed configuration. Local overrides take precedence where the consuming module uses the value. A setting's presence alone does not implement a feature.
- **Owner-confirmed:** a dated description of installed hardware or procedure. Usual arrangements may change by test; use that test's recorded setup when it differs.
- **Photographed:** a visible part/label in the supplied images. A nameplate rating is not a measured load, and visible wiring is not a complete circuit drawing.
- **Proposed / unverified:** an earlier suggestion, an interpretation, or a feature not established by the reviewed sources.
- **Unknown:** evidence is missing. These gaps are deliberately left open.

Source: knowledge_base/README.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Read these distinctions first

1. **Normal pre-cool ends at `probe_5 <= 5 °C`.** Probe 5 is usually attached to the underside of the upper aluminium tray. The historical 12 °C setting was for a shorter trial. Probe placement can change and must be recorded per test; neither threshold establishes thermal equilibrium of the whole camera.
2. The test covers **Qtec Hypervision variants**, both to establish reproducibility across units and to investigate design changes. There is no single fixed reference-camera revision. Record the unit, revision, focus/setup, and run settings for meaningful comparisons.
3. **Freezer on/camera off for cooling → freezer off → camera on for measurement.** Camera heat and intermittent lamp heat warm the chamber toward the endpoint. Normal operation never powers camera and freezer together. There is no controlled heater ramp or stability hold.
4. Analysis widths and shifts are in **pixels**. Signal and image-noise metrics are in **digital numbers (DN)**. The code does not establish calibrated spectral resolution in nm, temporal read noise, or acceptance limits.
5. Preflight and diagnostic scripts can switch real outputs. They are not all read-only checks. Do not run them alongside an acquisition.

## What FreezerTest does

FreezerTest automates temperature-dependent optical measurements of a camera using a freezer, temperature probes, a switched light source, and a motorized filter wheel. A host PC coordinates the apparatus and asks an embedded Linux camera computer to capture images. Offline analysis extracts image position, line/edge width, signal, and image-noise indicators, then compares their evolution within a test and across repeated tests.

The camera sits on an aluminium tray in the upper freezer. The target is **white PTFE with a black 3D-printed cage** to form sharp dark lines, illuminated by a **halogen tube and silver-coated parabolic reflector** focused onto the target. PTFE was chosen by the owner for reflection over the intended 400–1700 nm span; no calibrated reflectance standard is implied. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [hardware and photographs](02-hardware-and-connections.md).

The devices under test are **variants of the Qtec Hypervision camera family**, using Qtec computer logic and hardware. There is no single fixed reference-camera revision: multiple units of the same kind are tested to build evidence of reproducibility, while deliberate camera changes are also tested to investigate their consequences. The method and apparatus belong here; individual outcomes and development decisions remain outside this corpus. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

Qtec describes Hypervision as an Offner push-broom hyperspectral camera based on its C-series platform. The owner describes the relevant camera range as approximately 400–1700 nm; Qtec's current VIS-SWIR family documentation specifies 430–1700 nm. The exact configuration, detector, optics, and revision should be recorded for each tested unit rather than copied wholesale from a generic product page. See [Qtec Hypervision](https://docs.qtec.com/hsi/hypervision/intro/), [project context](08-project-context.md), and [hardware](02-hardware-and-connections.md).

Primary source: [long-test runner](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L441), [single sweep](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L201), [analysis configuration](../Config/analysis_config.py#L14), and [chat T2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#t2-freezer-camera-drift-analysis).

## Acquisition hierarchy

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Repeat sequence | A configured number of complete tests, with one shared repeat-group identifier |
| Test / repeat | One test folder containing pre-cool events, temperature logging, a measurement phase, and cleanup |
| Sweep | One ordered visit to all configured filter positions, normally producing four images plus metadata |
| Capture | One image at one filter position; filters are captured sequentially, not simultaneously |
| Analysis row | A per-sweep result assembled from available images, metrics, and associated temperatures |

This distinction matters: a filter-4 image is taken later than the filter-1 image in the same sweep. A sweep-associated temperature is not automatically the exact optical-component temperature at every individual exposure. See [data and metadata](05-data-and-metadata.md).

## Current implemented test concept

Normal preparation includes verifying filter positions before each long test and manually focusing on the target plane when changing cameras. The runner starts temperature logging, switches lamp and camera off, and runs the freezer until the selected pre-cool threshold is met; the owner-confirmed normal threshold is **`probe_5 <= 5 °C`**. The copied configuration used 12 °C for a shorter trial. A pre-cool timeout aborts the test. On successful pre-cool, the runner switches the freezer off, waits 60 seconds, powers the camera on, waits 45 seconds, and starts keepalive streaming when enabled. It then captures sweeps during warm-up until the selected endpoint logic ends measurement. The historical copied profile ends after three consecutive new records observed at `probe_5 >= 40 °C`, with a 14-hour measurement deadline checked between operations, and requests eight repeats. Blocking operations and the final sweep can extend that deadline. These trial-specific settings should not be treated as universal protocol requirements. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

The **camera and lamp supply the heat during measurement** after freezer power has been switched off. Normal operation never enables camera and freezer simultaneously. In the reviewed code the lamp is on during sweep captures and off between them, so its heating contribution is intermittent; the camera stays powered and streams between sweeps when keepalive is enabled. This describes the actual warming mechanism without implying a controlled heating rate or a continuously illuminated lamp. Routine camera shutdown is by cutting its power, as confirmed by the owner. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [sweep lamp sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L301).

In the usual probe arrangement, probes **1–3 measure the outer shell** (non-computer side, computer/hot side, and the side between them). Probe **4 is on the upper/camera-facing tray surface** and probe **5 is underneath the same tray**, both away from camera/lamp heat sources. Thus the usual pre-cool/end condition is based on **tray-underside temperature**, not a direct camera-core or free-air reading. Placements can change by test and the actual map must be recorded. [Usual probe map](02-hardware-and-connections.md#thermocouple-channels).

The runner does not command a controlled heating rate, establish thermal equilibrium at setpoints, or check humidity. These distinctions are central to interpreting temperature-associated measurements. See [running the test](04-running-the-test.md), [review gaps](09-review-questions-and-gaps.md), and [pre-cool code](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330).

## What the analysis can answer

- How spectral profile peak positions and FWHM change in image coordinates.
- How the selected spatial edge and its fitted line-spread width change.
- How selected signal-region mean DN and background-region spatial scatter change.
- How those metrics relate to associated external probe temperatures, selected internal camera temperatures, sweep index, and repeat identity. Recorded timestamps support additional time-based analysis, but the supplied viewers do not offer an elapsed-time axis.

The methodology does not, by itself, establish absolute wavelength accuracy, intrinsic spectrometer resolution independently of the bandpass filters, radiometric response, temporal noise, MTF, or a root cause of drift. It does not supply pass/fail specifications. [Analysis methodology](06-analysis-methodology.md) records the exact calculations and limits.

## System arrangement

The host PC runs the test coordinator, reads an Ethernet MCC temperature/DIO unit, commands a Tic stepper controller, and triggers image capture on the camera computer over SSH. The camera computer exposes a V4L2 video device and saves PNG images before transferring the sweep to the host. The freezer, lamp, and camera power are switched through the MCC digital outputs. The Hall home sensor is read through an MCC digital input. These are software relationships; cable routes and terminal numbers have not been established from a drawing. ### Manufacturer specifications and their limits

The owner's camera description is approximately **400–1700 nm**. Qtec's public Hypervision documentation lists its VIS-SWIR version as **430–1700 nm**, describes an Offner spectrograph, and places it on a Linux computer platform. Preserve these as separate owner and public-product descriptions: the public specifications do not establish the exact range, detector or revision of every camera tested here. Record the camera identity for each run, and perform the owner's stated manual focus adjustment when changing camera. [Qtec Hypervision documentation](https://docs.qtec.com/hsi/hypervision/intro/), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

Digilent identifies **6069-410-025** as **MCC E-TC**, with eight thermocouple inputs, 24-bit conversion, maximum 4 samples/s/channel and eight digital I/O. These are device capabilities, not the project's logging cadence or whole-chain accuracy. The code's logger requests a nominal 1 s interval. [Digilent E-TC product page](https://digilent.com/shop/mcc-e-tc-thermocouple-measurement-ethernet-daq-device/), [logger interval](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L21).

Pololu identifies item **3132** as the **Tic T834 with soldered connectors**, using a DRV8834 driver. Its manufacturer supply range is **2.5–10.8 V**, with approximately **1.5 A continuous per phase** without additional cooling. The owner confirms that the installed controller uses the **5 V rail**. The 24 V camera/contactor circuit is a separate supply arrangement. The photographed board also carries the **Tic T834** marking. [Pololu 3132](https://www.pololu.com/product/3132), [board photograph](reference/component-photos/IMG_5290.jpg), [29 October review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

## Chamber, illumination and thermal arrangement

The **Tefcold UF400V** nameplate shows **230 V, 50 Hz, 300 W, 2.5 A**, net volume **249 L**, and **R290 refrigerant, 80 g**. These are photographed appliance ratings, not measured running power or a verified chamber temperature specification. The camera sits on the **top face of an aluminium tray inside the freezer**; camera power and Ethernet leads and the thermocouple terminal bank are visible in the chamber photograph. [Freezer nameplate](reference/component-photos/IMG_5293.jpg), [chamber arrangement](reference/component-photos/IMG_5292.jpg), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

The owner identifies the optical test target as **white PTFE with a black 3D-printed cage**. A **silver-coated parabolic reflector** focuses the lamp's light. The lamp box is labelled **641840875, 24–28 V, 100 W, 118 mm R7S, ECO HALOGEN, 900 lm, 2000 h**; its brand is not visible. Lumens and service life are packaging ratings, not measured irradiance, spectrum or stability at the target. [Lamp packaging](reference/component-photos/IMG_5295.jpg), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

During the owner's normal test, the freezer cools with the camera off. At the cold threshold the freezer switches off, then camera power is enabled. **Heat from the camera and lamp warms the chamber toward the endpoint**; there is no dedicated controlled heater or commanded warming ramp in the supplied runner. The lamp is powered during sweep capture and switched off afterward, while the camera remains on between sweeps. The owner states that camera and freezer are never intentionally powered together during a normal run and accepts direct camera power removal as the normal shutdown method. This describes the test's operating practice, not a new guarantee from the power-switching hardware. [Pre-cool and camera start](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330), [lamp sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L299), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

Two dishes of orange beads, apparently desiccant, are visible below the tray. ## Digital input and output map

All four signals use the MCC `DigitalPortType.AUXPORT0`. A bit index is a software channel designation, not a connector pin number. [Port setup](../Control/temperature_control.py#L35).

| Logical function | AUXPORT0 bit | Direction | Active/on state | Inactive/off state | Where set |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| Lamp | 0 | Output | 1 | 0 | Hard-coded in `temperature_control.py` |
| Filterwheel Hall sensor | 1 | Input | 0 | Any value other than 0 evaluates inactive | Configured `HALL_DIO_BIT`, `HALL_ACTIVE_STATE` |
| Camera power relay | 2 | Output | 1 | 0 | Configured camera-power constants |
| Freezer contactor | 3 | Output | 1 | 0 | Configured freezer constants |

The camera and freezer active levels are configurable; their off levels are calculated as the inverse. Connecting the controller turns the lamp and freezer off and configures the camera-power bit as an output. The connection method does **not** explicitly turn camera power off at that point; the pre-cool workflow does this later. Disconnect attempts to turn the lamp, freezer and camera power off. [Connection behavior](../Control/temperature_control.py#L69), [signal read/write functions](../Control/temperature_control.py#L102), [disconnect](../Control/temperature_control.py#L168).

The recorded `lamp_state`, `freezer_state`, and `camera_power_state` represent the program's commanded state. There is no separate feedback measurement in this controller proving that the relay operated, power reached the load, the lamp emitted light, or the compressor ran. [State fields and readings](../Control/temperature_control.py#L199).

The owner identifies the thermocouples as **Omega 5SRTC-TT-KI-36-1M**. Omega lists that exact model as type K, **36 AWG / approximately 0.13 mm wire diameter**, **PFA insulation**, and **1 m lead length**; the 5SRTC style includes a miniature thermocouple plug and strain relief. These product details do not establish the physical placement or calibration of any particular probe. [Omega IEC series and exact model listing](https://www.jp.omega.com/pptst/5LSC_5SRTC_IEC.html).

The thermocouple connectors are **inside the freezer**, extended outside with **Labfacility XF-1275-FAR** KX wire, [Farnell order reference 2918721](https://dk.farnell.com/labfacility/xf-1275-far/thermocouple-wire-type-kx-10m/dp/2918721). The owner now identifies the DIN-rail terminal blocks through the **Omega DRTB-2 series** product link. That series has screw terminals and a built-in miniature female thermocouple connector, with variants for K, J and other thermocouple types. Type K is used in this test, but an exact fitted SKU such as **DRTB-K-2** has not been read from a label and should not be assumed solely from the series link. The terminal bank and plug connections are visible in the chamber. Actual extension lengths and termination details remain to be recorded. [Omega DRTB-2 series](https://www.dwyeromega.com/en-nl/thermocouple-din-rail-terminal-blocks-narrow-10-7-mm-width/p/DRTB-2), [chamber photograph](reference/component-photos/IMG_5292.jpg), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

| MCC channel | Logical probe name | Thermocouple type | Enabled in supplied configuration | Physical placement |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `probe_1` | K | Yes | Camera outer case on the side without the computer. |
| 1 | `probe_2` | K | Yes | Camera outer case on the computer side, described by the owner as the hot side. |
| 2 | `probe_3` | K | Yes | Side of the camera between the above two sides. |
| 3 | `probe_4` | K | Yes | Top, camera-facing surface of the aluminium tray, away from camera and lamp. |
| 4 | `probe_5` | K | Yes | Underside of the same tray, away from heat sources; normal pre-cool and measurement-end reference. |
| 5 | `probe_6` | K | No | Unconfirmed |
| 6 | `probe_7` | K | No | Unconfirmed |
| 7 | `probe_8` | K | No | Unconfirmed |

Sources: [channel map](../Config/temperature_config.py#L12), [29 October owner placement description](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026). These are the **usual placements**, which may change with test configuration. Record exceptions with each run. Probes 1–3 measure case surfaces; probes 4–5 measure tray surfaces. In particular, `probe_5` is not a direct chamber-air or internal-optics temperature measurement. Its selected role as the endpoint sensor is a protocol choice.

The owner reports **5 °C at probe 5** as the normal cold threshold and explains that **12 °C** was used recently to shorten testing. The archived local configuration contains 12 °C. These are protocol choices, not probe specifications or verified temperatures of the optics; retain the actual selected threshold with each test. [Owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [configuration snapshot](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L27).

At connection, the controller sets a thermocouple type for every entry, including disabled channels. During a read it skips disabled channels, asks the device for Celsius values, and records `ULException` errors per probe. It does not apply a project-specific offset or scale correction in this code. Factory/device calibration and cold-junction behavior must be documented from the actual MCC model and its setup rather than inferred here. [Type setup](../Control/temperature_control.py#L77), [temperature reading](../Control/temperature_control.py#L210).

The default logger interval is 1 s, with a sleep after each reading cycle, so this is a nominal cadence rather than a guaranteed exact 1 Hz sample clock. [Logger defaults](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L21), [logger loop](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L79).

### Mechanical reference and Hall arrangement

The owner confirms that the **Hall sensor is attached to the fixed base** and the **magnet is on the rotating part**. The supplied datasheet is Honeywell's **SL353 series micropower omnipolar digital Hall sensor**, covering **SL353HT** and **SL353LT**. It specifies a **2.2–5.5 V** operating supply, **−40 to +85 °C** operation, and a **push-pull output** that goes low with an activating magnetic field and high when it is removed. That logic agrees with the configured active-low read. Either magnetic pole can activate the device. [Honeywell datasheet supplied via RS, pp. 2–4](https://docs.rs-online.com/9a79/A700000007013601.pdf), [Hall configuration](../Config/system_config.py#L25).

The exact fitted **HT/LT suffix remains unknown**: the nominal sampling periods differ (45 microseconds for HT versus 45 milliseconds for LT at the datasheet's nominal conditions). Record the actual suffix and interface wiring when documenting the homing response; no sensor-response/repeatability validation is inferred from the family datasheet. Its IC pin diagram is not an as-built pin map for the rig.

Six supplied STL files are preserved in the [filterwheel CAD inventory](reference/filterwheel-cad/README.md), with a preview below. The meshes provide mechanical reference; their assembled roles, exact current-build correspondence and dimensions should be established from the inventory and owner review rather than guessed from filenames or this preview.

![Independent views of the six supplied filterwheel CAD meshes](assets/filterwheel-cad-overview.png)

The motor's photographed label resolves the earlier generic NEMA 17 identity to **SY42STH38-1684B**. The label does not give phase current, winding resistance or step angle, so those values are not inferred from the suffix. [Motor photograph](reference/component-photos/IMG_5289.jpg).

Current coordinator settings are step mode `8`, current limit `1500 mA`, max speed `4000000`, starting speed `0`, max acceleration/deceleration `40000`, position tolerance `5`, settle time `0.2 s`, and move timeout `10 s`. Speed and acceleration numbers are passed directly to `ticcmd`; this knowledge base does not convert their units without the actual controller documentation. Class constructor defaults differ from the coordinator configuration, so use the passed configuration when interpreting production behavior. [Configured values](../Config/system_config.py#L10), [driver constructor](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L13), [coordinator passes settings](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L241).

The controller is energized for motion, then de-energized at idle and during image capture by default to reduce stepper heating. During homing it stays energized between the search steps. De-energization is an intended thermal behavior; whether the wheel can drift while unpowered must be checked physically. Controller-reported position is not an independent measurement of optical alignment. [Move behavior](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L119), [homing current behavior](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L172).

Source: knowledge_base/02-hardware-and-connections.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Hall homing

With the normal configuration, home search direction is `-1`, coarse increment `50`, fine increment `1`, and maximum coarse travel counter `3000`. The algorithm:

1. If Hall is already active, move away until inactive.
2. Search coarsely toward the magnet until Hall becomes active.
3. Move away in fine increments until inactive.
4. Approach in fine increments until the active edge is found, then set Tic position to zero.

The result records the starting, coarse-hit, inactive-edge and final-edge positions plus duration. The 3000 counter limits the initial move-away and coarse-search stages. The fine back-away/approach loops do not have their own travel or elapsed-time bound in this implementation. A successful software home therefore establishes a sensor-edge reference, not an independently measured repeatability specification. [Homing configuration](../Config/system_config.py#L25), [homing implementation](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L158).

## Camera internal temperature channels and TEC

There are two sources of internal readings:

- `sensors -j` supplies whatever hardware-monitor sensors exist on the camera computer. The program maps driver families to friendly names such as CPU, GPU, FPGA, Sensor PCB and PCB. These names are software labels, not proof that every component exists or is measured at the exact location implied by a label.
- V4L2 supplies `sensor_temperature`; the program treats its integer value as millidegrees Celsius and divides by 1000, then rounds to 0.1 °C. It also reads `temperature_control` and records a Boolean when parseable. It does not set or regulate a TEC setpoint.

The camera-side code states that this camera's sensor-temperature control updates only while video is actively streaming. It therefore keeps a temporary stream alive while reading, or uses the existing keepalive stream. An exactly 20.0 °C camera reading receives a possible-default/stale warning; that is a diagnostic flag, not evidence that all 20 °C readings are invalid. [Refresh rationale](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L152), [warning](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L327).

## Software layers

The host PC owns sequencing, MCC I/O, wheel movement, temperature logging, data transfer, and analysis. The camera computer owns the V4L2 video device, image-capture pipeline, and internal temperature queries. Camera-side Python modules are deployed separately; editing the local copy does not update the running camera. [Sweep orchestration](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L201), [camera deployment](../Scripts/deploy_camera_scripts.sh#L7).

| File or group | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Config/system_config.py` | Base host configuration: motion, DIO, network endpoints, control features, test timing, recovery and metadata; imports local overrides at the end. |
| `Config/local_config.py` | Site/run overrides, including the required local results path. The original copied profile is preserved as historical evidence; its trial settings are not the normal protocol. |
| `Config/temperature_config.py` | MCC network endpoint and thermocouple channel definitions; imported directly by the temperature controller. |
| `Config/analysis_config.py` | Filter identities, nominal wavelengths/widths, image ROIs and analysis options; imported directly by analysis. |
| `Control/temperature_control.py` | MCC connection, thermocouple readings, Hall input, lamp/freezer/camera output switching. |
| `Control/temperature_logger.py` | Background nominal 1 s logging, latest-record access and forwarding control methods through one owned controller. |
| `Control/filterwheel_control.py` | Calls `ticcmd`, sets motion/current parameters, moves to positions, Hall homing and shutdown. |
| `Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py` | Starts, checks and stops a remote camera stream to `/dev/null`; captures process/event details. |
| `Scripts/run_long_test.py` | Repeated tests, pre-cool, camera power sequence, stop conditions, scheduled sweeps, storage checks, event/summary files and bounded camera recovery. |
| `Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py` | One wheel sweep, optional homing, illumination timing, internal camera readings, per-filter remote capture, transfer and local presence checks. |
| `Camera_scripts/camera_config.py` | Camera-side video format, resolution, frame rate, default exposure and gain. |
| `Camera_scripts/camera_control.py` | Applies V4L2 settings, runs a one-frame GStreamer PNG pipeline, checks file existence/size, and writes per-image metadata. |
| `Camera_scripts/capture_remote.py` | Camera-side entry point accepting output path and optional exposure-control value. |
| `Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py` | Camera-side JSON readout from `sensors -j` and V4L2, including temporary-stream refresh. |
| `Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py` | Single-test image metrics, temperature columns, CSVs, plots and profile diagnostics. |
| `Scripts/preview_analysis_rois.py` | Image/ROI previews used to review analysis regions. |
| `Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py` | Batch single-test analysis, cross-cycle diagnostics and repeatability summaries. |
| `Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit.py` | Interactive comparison application with metadata editing. |
| `Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py` | A second comparison implementation with expanded test/repeat-group browsing. The authoritative entry point needs owner confirmation. |

The analysis methods and data interpretation belong to the analysis chapter; this chapter records their software entry points and environment requirements.

## Configuration precedence

`Config/system_config.py` defines base values, then performs `from Config.local_config import *` inside an `ImportError` handler. Therefore the supplied local values win for consumers that import from `Config.system_config`. Editing a base value with an existing local override will not change the effective value. [Override mechanism](../Config/system_config.py#L169).

Important boundaries:

- `Config/temperature_config.py` and `Config/analysis_config.py` are separate configurations; the wildcard import does not replace the direct imports from those modules.
- The camera imports `camera_config.py` on the camera computer. Host overrides are not automatically shared with it. The host explicitly passes each filter's exposure value to the camera capture entry point.
- Many constants are imported by value when a program starts. Restart the appropriate process after changing configuration; do not expect live reload.
- `LOCAL_DATA_ROOT` is defined only in the supplied `local_config.py`, although acquisition/preflight import it from `system_config.py`. Removing the local file does not produce a complete working base-only configuration. Its current path refers to a different Linux user's home directory; choose a reviewed, writable results location on the intended host.

For normal operation, the owner specifies cooling until **`probe_5` is at or below 5 °C**, then switching the freezer off before the camera starts. The copied profile's **12 °C** threshold was deliberately chosen for a shorter recent trial. ### Thermal sequence and probe meaning

The owner confirms the normal sequence: **freezer on / camera off** while cooling to the 5 °C threshold, then freezer off, the configured 60 s settle, camera on, and its configured 45 s boot wait. The camera and freezer are never on together during normal operation. Heat from the operating camera and the lamp warms the chamber during measurement toward the selected end temperature. This is the intended warm-up mechanism; the runner does not drive a separate heater or command a closed-loop temperature ramp. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [pre-cool and freezer-off](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330), [camera startup](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L559).

The lamp's contribution is **intermittent in the reviewed software**: each managed sweep switches it on, waits 2 s, captures the configured filter images (normally four), then switches it off. It is not held on throughout the measurement phase. The owner's camera-and-lamp thermal description therefore does not imply continuous lamp power in this source revision. [Lamp sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L299), [lamp off](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L344).

The usual `probe_5` placement is on the underside of an aluminium tray in the upper freezer, away from camera and lamp heat; `probe_4` is on the camera-facing top of that tray. Probes 1–3 are on the camera case. These placements can change between tests, so record the actual map rather than treating a probe label as a permanent physical quantity. In particular, `probe_5` is not a free-air or camera-core reading. See [the usual probe map](02-hardware-and-connections.md#thermocouple-channels) and [operator preparation](04-running-the-test.md#operator-preparation). [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

## Camera capture configuration and behavior

| Camera-side setting | Supplied value |
|---|---|
| Video device | `/dev/video4` |
| Frame size | 1296 × 1032 pixels |
| Pixel format | `GRAY8` |
| Frame rate | 24 frames/s requested |
| Gain | 0 requested |
| Default exposure control | `exposure_time_absolute=20000` |
| Image staging root | `/root/scripts/data` |
| Configured log root | `/root/scripts/logs`; the capture controller shown here does not itself use `LOG_ROOT` |

Source: [camera configuration](../Camera_scripts/camera_config.py#L2).

The host normally overrides exposure per filter: 3000, 15000, 8000 and 15000 for filters 1–4 respectively. A missing mapping uses host `DEFAULT_EXPOSURE_TIME_ABSOLUTE=20000`. The optional CLI argument to `capture_remote.py` takes precedence over the camera-side default. These numbers are driver-control values; unit/range confirmation remains open. [Exposure settings](../Config/system_config.py#L148), [CLI override](../Camera_scripts/capture_remote.py#L16).

Before each frame, the camera program applies requested frame rate, exposure and gain through `v4l2-ctl`, waits 0.1 s, and queries settings. It then runs `gst-launch-1.0 -e` with `v4l2src num-buffers=1`, raw `GRAY8` caps, `pngenc`, and `filesink`. The output is one PNG from an 8-bit grayscale input pipeline, plus a JSON sidecar. This does not establish the sensor's native bit depth or record higher-bit raw samples. [Settings](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L80), [pipeline](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L106).

The sidecar records requested and before/after applied exposure/gain, stream parameters, image dimensions and encoding, capture status, file size, timestamp and the pipeline command. Success requires a nonempty image file. It does not include an image-content/saturation/alignment acceptance check at capture time. The timestamp is recorded before launching the pipeline, not a hardware exposure timestamp. [Capture verification and metadata](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L126).

## Streaming and internal-temperature configuration

The copied local profile enables a long `v4l2-ctl --stream-mmap` stream on `/dev/video4`, with `100000000` requested frames, 2 s startup wait, frames discarded to `/dev/null`, PID file `/tmp/freezertest_keepalive_stream.pid`, and log file `/tmp/freezertest_keepalive_stream.log`. It is finite by frame count, despite being called continuous/keepalive. The code tests process existence for status, not actual frame progress or sensor freshness. [Settings](../Config/system_config.py#L99), [historical local enablement](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L36), [status](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L91), [launch](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L126).

Normal capture shares the same video node, so the sweep reads internal temperatures while the keepalive is active, stops it, waits 2 s for buffers/device release, captures all filters, then restarts it and reads temperatures again. The sweep avoids starting a second refresh stream if a keepalive object was supplied. [Sweep sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L282).

Keepalive startup can terminate stale matching `v4l2-ctl` streams to `/dev/null`, including streams whose PID file was lost. This is useful cleanup but matters if someone is using another such diagnostic stream on the camera. Stop first requests termination and waits about 3 s, then force-kills if necessary. [Stale cleanup](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L134), [stop](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L184).

For reads without keepalive, the temporary sensor-refresh stream requests 300 frames and waits 1 s before reading `sensor_temperature` while the stream remains running. Internal temperature collection is enabled but non-fatal: the sweep retains failure/error details and continues capture. A successful remote JSON read can still contain sensor-specific errors, so inspect `remote_payload.errors` and per-sensor warnings rather than relying on outer `status=success`. [Refresh configuration](../Config/system_config.py#L88), [temporary stream](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L152), [host wrapper](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L81), [combined payload](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L335).

## What a run does

The main entry point is `Scripts/run_long_test.py`. For each configured repeat it creates a separate test folder, starts continuous MCC temperature logging, pre-cools with the camera off, turns the freezer off, starts the camera and optional continuous stream, collects periodic filter sweeps, and shuts down the controlled outputs. The next repeat starts a fresh pre-cool cycle. **The camera and freezer are never on together in normal operation.** During measurement the freezer stays off; heat from the camera and lamp warms the chamber toward the end-temperature condition. The runner commands no separate heater or closed-loop temperature ramp. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [run setup](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L441), [pre-cool](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L287), [measurement startup](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L537), [repeat loop](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L1025).

```text
Initialize folder and logger
  → Wait for a valid pre-cool probe reading
  → Camera/lamp off; freezer on
  → Pre-cool threshold reached; freezer off; timed settle
  → Camera on; boot wait; keepalive stream if enabled
  → Measurement clock starts
  → Camera heat + sweep-switched lamp warm the chamber
  → Sweep → wait interval → sweep … until end condition/stop/failure
  → Stop stream; freezer off; lamp off; camera off; stop logger
  → Inter-repeat delay → next repeat
```

The diagram represents the normal path when the relevant control features are enabled. Normal pre-cool ends when `probe_5` reaches **5 °C or below**. The lamp is on for each sweep's 2 s warm-up and image loop, then off between sweeps; it is not continuously on during the thermal warm-up phase. Pre-cooling can be skipped by configuration, sweeps can fail, and stop requests or timeouts can interrupt the path. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [lamp control](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L299).

1. Identify the camera under test, including its family variant and individual unit. The setup supports Qtec Hypervision variants rather than one fixed reference camera. Keep the same-type unit comparison and evaluation of a camera change identifiable in the run context.

6. Check the intended pre-cool threshold, camera identity/operator/notes, capture settings, storage path, and stop-file state before the preflight/acquisition sequence.

## Starting a run

These commands are verified from the source entry points; they were **not executed against hardware** while preparing this knowledge base. Run them from the repository root in the configured acquisition environment.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/preflight_check.py
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/run_long_test.py
```

Preflight is a separate command. The long-test runner does not automatically run it. Its default checks are camera and MCC ping, camera SSH, remote capture-script/data-folder presence, `ticcmd` availability/device/status, local storage write/free space, and an MCC temperature/Hall read. It exits with status 1 if any check fails. [Source: preflight main](../Scripts/preflight_check.py#L275).

**Preflight operates real outputs.** Its MCC check connects a `TemperatureController`; connection switches the lamp and enabled freezer output off, and disconnection attempts lamp/freezer/camera power off. Consequently, even default preflight must not be treated as a passive diagnostic to run during acquisition. Optional flags add a real capture, deleted afterward, or a brief lamp toggle. [Sources: MCC check](../Scripts/preflight_check.py#L185), [connect](../Control/temperature_control.py#L69), [disconnect](../Control/temperature_control.py#L168), [optional checks](../Scripts/preflight_check.py#L107), [optional lamp](../Scripts/preflight_check.py#L223).

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/preflight_check.py --test-camera-capture --test-lamp
```

The camera deployment helper is `bash Scripts/deploy_camera_scripts.sh`. It copies `capture_remote.py`, `camera_control.py`, `camera_config.py`, and `read_camera_temperatures.py` to `/root/scripts/`, then creates the remote `data` and `logs` subfolders. It has its own hard-coded camera address/user and assumes `/root/scripts/` already exists for the copy step. Check those before using it; editing host configuration alone does not update the helper. [Source: deployment script](../Scripts/deploy_camera_scripts.sh#L4).

Source: knowledge_base/04-running-the-test.md

## Pre-cooling and the start of measurement

1. Start the MCC logger with a requested 1 s interval, before pre-cool and before measurement timing begins.
2. Wait up to 60 s for a value from `PRECOOL_SENSOR_NAME`. This wait occurs even if pre-cooling will subsequently be skipped.
3. When pre-cooling and freezer control are enabled, attempt lamp off and camera off, then freezer on. Errors while forcing lamp/camera off are printed and do not themselves stop pre-cooling.
4. Poll the latest logger record until selected temperature ≤ target; normal settings are **`probe_5` ≤5 °C**. This is one threshold crossing, **not a temperature stability window or soak hold**. If the probe is already at/below target, pre-cool may finish almost immediately after freezer-on.
5. Switch freezer off and wait the fixed settle duration.
6. Power camera on when enabled, wait 45 s by default, then start keepalive if enabled. Failure to establish keepalive at measurement startup aborts the test.
7. Only now set `measurement_start_time`, calculate the end deadline, and allow the first sweep immediately.

Sources: [first record](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L266), [pre-cool sequence](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L287), [measurement startup](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L537), [boot wait](../Config/system_config.py#L34), [measurement clock](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L586).

The owner confirms that the operating camera and lamp provide the heat for the measurement warm-up with freezer power off. In the supplied code the camera remains powered during this phase, while the lamp is switched only for sweep capture. No lamp duty-cycle change or extra heater is implied by the thermal description. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [sweep lamp sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L299).

There is no explicit probe-freshness limit, stability slope check, or finite-number validation in the threshold helper: it converts the selected value with `float()`. Pre-cool polls the latest available record rather than requiring a new record on each poll. Confirm that logged readings are advancing when interpreting a run. [Sources: conversion helper](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L118), [pre-cool loop](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L352).

## What happens during one sweep

Each long-test sweep receives the logger's latest external-temperature record, Hall reader, lamp callbacks, and optional keepalive object. Its normal sequence is:

1. Create a local sweep folder and matching temporary camera-side folder.
2. Initialize filter-wheel controller. If enabled, home using the Hall input and the configured search parameters.
3. Read internal camera temperatures with label `before_capture`.
4. Stop keepalive before capture, if configured, and wait the default 2 s for video-device buffers to release.
5. Switch lamp on and wait the default 2 s warm-up.
6. Visit filters in ascending numerical order. For each: move to configured target, read actual controller position, select per-filter exposure or default exposure, and invoke the remote PNG capture.
7. In the capture cleanup block, switch lamp off, restart keepalive if configured, and read internal camera temperatures with label `after_capture`.
8. Return wheel to zero and read its final position on successful capture path. Shutdown of the wheel controller is attempted in the outer `finally` block, including on failure.
9. Write local `sweep_summary.json`, copy the remote folder to local disk, check for all expected filenames, and only then remove the remote folder.
10. Write transfer timing. The long-test runner then adds its latest `temperature_after_sweep` record to the summary.

Sources: [sweep arguments and folder creation](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L201), [initialization and capture](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L256), [capture cleanup](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L344), [return/shutdown/transfer](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L364), [long-run after-sweep record](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L819).

One image per filter is captured by a GStreamer pipeline using `v4l2src` with `num-buffers=1` and `pngenc`. Camera settings are applied before capture, and requested/applied settings are recorded in an image sidecar. The copied camera configuration requests 1296 × 1032 pixels, `GRAY8`, 24 frames/s, and gain 0. There is no image averaging or multi-frame selection in this capture function. [Sources: camera configuration](../Camera_scripts/camera_config.py#L2), [settings and pipeline](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L80).

Source: knowledge_base/04-running-the-test.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Timing and end conditions

| Mechanism | Implemented meaning |
|---|---|
| Sweep interval | After every attempt, the runner schedules the next normal sweep for current time + interval. Capture, homing, internal-temperature reads, transfer, and cleanup add to start-to-start spacing. This is not a fixed 120 s sampling grid. |
| Time mode | Ends when elapsed measurement time reaches `TEST_DURATION_HOURS`, checked between sweep attempts/waits. No extra endpoint sweep is requested in this branch. |
| Temperature mode | Ends when selected probe meets inclusive `above` (≥ target) or `below` (≤ target) condition for the required count of new records observed by the runner. A nonmeeting or missing-value record resets the count. |
| Record uniqueness | Uses the temperature record's `timestamp` to avoid repeatedly counting one record; falls back to object identity when timestamp is missing. |
| Temperature safety timeout | Uses `TEST_END_SAFETY_TIMEOUT_HOURS` from measurement start. Does not include pre-cool, settle, or camera boot time. |
| Endpoint images | When enabled in temperature mode, threshold or timeout forces an immediate final sweep regardless of next normal trigger. Completion follows a successful final sweep. Failures can cause further attempts, until another stopping condition intervenes. |
| Maximum sweeps | Caps numbered attempts. Failed sweeps increment the index too. Reaching the cap can complete a test before the temperature target. |

Sources: [end-mode helpers](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L133), [record identity](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L163), [deadlines](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L590), [end logic](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L681), [consecutive observations](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L733), [rescheduling/max attempts](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L919).

The runner does not examine the end-condition temperature during a blocking sweep or transfer. “Three consecutive reads” means consecutive **new records observed by this loop**, not necessarily every record written by the logger. The 14 h deadline is a logical measurement deadline, not a guaranteed wall-clock cutoff: a current operation, recovery, or requested endpoint sweep can extend it. For example, SSH capture has a 60 s host timeout, but `scp` is invoked without a subprocess timeout. [Sources: measurement loop](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L646), [remote capture timeout](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L71), [copy implementation](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L157).

`completed` alone does not prove target temperature was reached. Inspect `completion_reason`: `time_limit`, `temperature_target`, `temperature_safety_timeout`, or `max_sweeps`. [Sources: time completion](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L685), [temperature completion](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L778), [post-sweep completion](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L932).

## Keepalive and internal-temperature behavior

Keepalive runs a remote `v4l2-ctl` memory-mapped video stream to `/dev/null`, retaining no image file. Its purpose in the code is to keep the camera/TEC/video pipeline active between sweeps; it is not an independent implementation of temperature regulation. PID and log files live under `/tmp` by default. Starting it can terminate stale `v4l2-ctl` streams to `/dev/null` on that camera. [Sources: rationale](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L4), [start command](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L126), [configured files](../Config/system_config.py#L99).

Because keepalive and PNG capture use the same V4L2 device, keepalive normally stops before image capture and restarts afterward. Stop first sends a normal termination, waits about 3 s, and may force termination. The status check establishes that a PID is alive; it does not inspect frame content or prove streaming health. Startup at measurement begin and after camera recovery requires `running=True`; ordinary post-sweep restart events are saved but are not explicitly rejected by the sweep if `running=False`. [Sources: status](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L91), [stop](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L184), [sweep restart](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L350), [startup enforcement](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L571).

Without a keepalive object, the camera-temperature script may briefly stream so `sensor_temperature` updates while it is read. With a keepalive object, sweeps request no temporary refresh to avoid a second stream on the same device. Internal-temperature reads are nonfatal: missing script, SSH trouble, or unavailable sensor records produce failure/error information in the sweep summary while image acquisition may continue. A wrapper status of `success` means JSON was received; inspect the payload's `errors` too. [Sources: wrapper](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L81), [refresh selection](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L282), [camera sensor reading](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L248).

## Stops, repeats, and cleanup

| Operator action | Scope and behavior |
|---|---|
| Create `STOP` inside the current test folder | Checked during pre-cool and at measurement loop boundaries. During measurement, marks `stopped_by_user`; it does not necessarily prevent the main repeat loop from starting the next repeat. During pre-cool it raises an error and records pre-cool failure. |
| Create `STOP_REPEAT` in `LOCAL_DATA_ROOT` (or configured stop filename) | Stops the active measurement at a loop boundary and prevents the next repeat. Also checked during pre-cool and between repeats. |
| Remove old stop files before a new intended sequence | Existing root-level repeat-stop file prevents any repeat from starting. The runner does not delete it automatically. |

Sources: [stop-file helpers](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L96), [pre-cool checks](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L352), [measurement checks](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L646), [repeat-delay and main loop](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L1006).

Stop files do not interrupt an image capture, transfer, recovery power-cycle, fixed settle, or boot wait in progress. Between repeats, the stop file is checked in chunks up to 60 s. [Sources: boot wait](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L559), [recovery waits](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L231), [repeat delay](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L1006).

Normal and exception cleanup attempt, in order, keepalive stop, freezer off, lamp off, optional explicit camera off, then logger stop. Output-command failures are recorded or printed. These are attempts through software control, not physical feedback proving contacts opened. The logger's own stop/disconnect path also attempts camera power off, so setting `CAMERA_POWER_OFF_AT_TEST_END=False` does **not** reliably keep the camera on in the supplied implementation. Abrupt process termination, host power loss, or broken communication cannot be assumed to execute cleanup. [Sources: runner cleanup](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L959), [logger stop](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L44), [controller disconnect](../Control/temperature_control.py#L168).

**Routine camera shutdown is by removing its power.** The owner confirms this as the accepted procedure for the rig, matching the relay-based shutdown in the runner. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [camera power-off call](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L988).

Ctrl-C raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, which bypasses the runner's `except Exception` status handlers. Its `finally` cleanup is still attempted, but a saved summary can remain `running` or `precooling` without a terminal status or `end_time`. Use the documented stop-file path for a normal recorded stop; the status left in a folder is not by itself proof that a process is still running. [Exception and cleanup path](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L945).

## Failures and recovery

Storage is checked initially and after each attempted sweep against the default 5 GiB free threshold (calculated with 1024³ bytes). It is not a continuous disk monitor while a sweep is capturing/transferring. Low space raises an error. [Sources: storage check](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L73), [post-attempt check](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L919), [threshold](../Config/system_config.py#L142).

Ordinary sweep errors increment both failed-attempt count and consecutive failures. The default retry wait is 30 s; afterward the normal post-attempt sweep interval is also scheduled, so ordinary retry timing is longer than 30 s. Three consecutive ordinary failures abort by default. Successful capture resets the streak. [Sources: failure handling](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L853), [rescheduling](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L919), [defaults](../Config/system_config.py#L142).

Automatic camera recovery matches a small set of error strings: required-memory allocation, buffer-pool activation, `VIDIOC_REQBUFS`, and device/resource-busy errors. With recovery enabled, it stops keepalive, forces lamp off, powers **only the camera** off, waits 15 s by default, powers it on, waits 45 s, and restarts keepalive. The MCC logger and host process continue; freezer control is unchanged and the freezer is normally off during measurement. Up to three recoveries per test are configured by default; a successful recovery resets ordinary failure streak and schedules the next numbered sweep immediately. The failed attempt remains a failure; recovery does not recreate that same sweep index. [Sources: markers](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L176), [recovery procedure](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L191), [recovery decision](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L864), [recovery defaults](../Config/system_config.py#L41).

Capture failure can leave images on the camera because transfer/removal happens only after the successful sweep block. Transfer verification checks expected filename existence, not checksums or PNG decodability. A transfer/removal failure can leave a local `sweep_summary.json` already marked `success` while the test-level event records that the attempt failed. Review both levels and file integrity before treating a partial sweep as usable. [Source: summary and transfer ordering](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L364).

## Storage hierarchy

Long-test outputs are written under `LOCAL_DATA_ROOT`. Temporary image files are first written under `REMOTE_DATA_ROOT` on the camera, then copied to the acquisition host. The supplied local configuration selects `/home/henrik/Documents/FreezerTest_Results`; camera-side base configuration selects `/root/scripts/data`. These paths describe the copied acquisition profile, not the documentation folder on this computer. [Sources: local root](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L5), [remote root](../Config/system_config.py#L116), [sweep paths](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L214).

```text
<LOCAL_DATA_ROOT>/
├── STOP_REPEAT                         optional operator-created sequence-stop file
└── <camera_id>_repeat_001_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>/
    ├── test_metadata.json
    ├── test_summary.json
    ├── test_log.jsonl
    ├── temperature_log.jsonl
    ├── STOP                            optional operator-created test-stop file
    └── sweep_0001_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>/
        ├── sweep_summary.json
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_1.png
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_1.json
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_2.png
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_2.json
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_3.png
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_3.json
        ├── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_4.png
        └── <YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_filter_4.json
```

For a single configured repeat, the long-test root omits `_repeat_001`: `<camera_id>_<timestamp>`. The standalone sweep command instead creates `manual_test_<timestamp>`. Camera IDs are sanitized to letters, digits, underscore, period, and hyphen; unsupported runs of characters become underscores. [Sources: camera-safe name](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L62), [root naming](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L429), [manual root](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L421).

JSON files contain one formatted JSON object. JSONL files contain one JSON object per line and may be read incrementally during a run. Expected files vary when filters are reconfigured; the current four-filter expectation follows sorted `FILTER_POSITIONS` keys rather than a separate hard-coded file list. [Sources: JSON/event writing](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L104), [expected sweep files](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L179).

## Test metadata fields

The initial `test_metadata.json` contains the following groups. It records selected settings, **not a complete snapshot of every effective configuration value**. [Source: object creation](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L464).

| Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `camera_id`, `operator`, `notes` | Explicit context from configuration; identity strings are not inferred from the captured image |
| `test_date`, `folder_created_at` | Date/time the repeat folder is created, before pre-cool; not measurement-start time |
| `test_duration_hours` | Configured time-mode duration, present even when temperature mode is selected |
| `test_end_mode`, `test_end_sensor`, `test_end_target_c`, `test_end_direction` | Chosen measurement termination rule |
| `test_end_safety_timeout_hours`, `test_end_required_consecutive_reads`, `test_end_final_sweep_enabled` | Temperature-mode deadline/confirmation/endpoint behavior |
| `repeat_index`, `repeat_count` | Position in configured repeat sequence and configured sequence length; a failed/stopped sequence may produce fewer folders |
| `repeat_group_id`, `repeat_group_start_date` | Link repeat folders to one sequence start |
| `precool_enabled`, `precool_sensor`, `precool_target_c` | Selected pre-cool configuration |
| `camera_keepalive_stream_enabled`, `camera_auto_recovery_enabled`, `camera_auto_recovery_max_per_test` | Selected runtime stream/recovery configuration |

The current runner derives `repeat_group_id` as `<safe_camera_id>_<YYYY-MM-DD>` from sequence start, then gives every repeat in that invocation the same ID. It is not guaranteed unique if two sequences for the same camera start on the same date. Older repair tools can produce different group formats, so do not infer precise grouping solely from a string pattern. [Sources: group ID](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L69), [main sequence](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L1025), [older repair format](../Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py#L137).

The owner uses the apparatus both for reproducibility across same-type camera units and for investigating design changes. Record a unique unit identity plus its tested revision/configuration, change under investigation, actual pre-cool threshold, verified wheel positions, and manual focus/setup state. Existing `camera_id` and `notes` can carry some of this context, but the runner does not create dedicated structured fields for every item. Do not treat the family name as a unique unit/revision ID or pool different revisions as an unchanged population. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [analysis comparisons](06-analysis-methodology.md#repeat-cycle-comparison).

Also record the **actual probe-placement map for each test**. The usual arrangement is shell probes 1–3, tray upper surface probe 4 and tray underside probe 5, but the owner can move probes between experiments. The numeric `probe_n` labels alone do not encode placement; the runner does not automatically store the map. Use the existing notes or an accompanying setup record. The PTFE/cage target, focus, halogen/reflector arrangement and camera/lamp-driven warming form part of that setup context. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

## Test summary and event log

`test_summary.json` starts with status `initializing`, changes to `precooling` and `running`, then may finish as `completed`, `stopped_by_user`, or `aborted`. It stores `completed_sweeps` and `failed_sweeps`, initial storage information, configured limits, and an `events` array. Events are appended to both `test_log.jsonl` and the summary; the latter also gains `last_update` on each append. [Sources: initial summary](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L492), [append mechanism](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L109), [status transitions](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L537), [termination](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L945).

Additional fields appear as execution progresses:

- `precool_result`: assigned after completed or skipped pre-cool; successful pre-cool includes target/sensor/final temperature, duration, freezer on/off records, and last temperature record. A failed pre-cool appends a `precool_failed` event and raises before this field is assigned.
- `measurement_start_time`, `planned_end_time`, `planned_end_time_type`: measurement-phase timing, created after pre-cool, settle, camera boot, and optional stream startup.
- `end_time`, `completion_reason`: actual loop termination time/reason. `completed` can mean temperature target, time limit, temperature safety timeout, or maximum attempts; inspect the reason.
- `fatal_error`: text when the test aborts through an ordinary exception.
- `camera_keepalive_stream_events`, `camera_auto_recovery_count`, `camera_auto_recovery_events`: stream lifecycle and successful camera-recovery information recorded by the runner.
- `final_freezer_off_record`, `final_lamp_off_record`, `camera_power_off_record` or associated error fields: cleanup command outcomes/latest readbacks. They are not relay-contact feedback measurements.

Sources: [pre-cool results](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L398), [pre-cool result assignment](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L550), [measurement timing](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L604), [completion/fatal errors](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L932), [cleanup fields](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L959).

An interrupted process can leave a nonterminal summary. In particular, Ctrl-C (`KeyboardInterrupt`) bypasses the `except Exception` status handler while still entering cleanup, so `status` can remain `precooling` or `running` without an `end_time`. Distinguish an incomplete record from a currently active process; compare the process state and logs rather than relying solely on that field. [Exception/cleanup handling](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L945).

The JSONL event stream includes `event_type` for pre-cool, stop, and end-condition records. Sweep-attempt events instead include `sweep_index`, `trigger_reason`, `status`, and temperature/path/error fields; do not assume every log object has `event_type`. A sweep event is constructed as `started` but appended after the attempt, when it is usually `success` or `failed`. Its original `timestamp` is retained, so file append order/time and event timestamp have different meanings. [Sources: pre-cool event](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L321), [sweep event construction](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L806), [event append after attempt](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L919).

## External temperature log schema

Normal `temperature_log.jsonl` records contain:

| Field | Type/meaning |
|---|---|
| `timestamp` | Host local ISO timestamp created before controller reads the enabled channels |
| `temperatures_c` | Object mapping enabled probe names to successfully returned temperatures in °C |
| `errors` | Object mapping probe names to individual MCC read error text |
| `lamp_state` | Controller's last commanded logical lamp state |
| `freezer_state` | Controller's last commanded logical freezer state |
| `camera_power_state` | Controller's last commanded camera state, possibly `null` before a command |
| `logger_timestamp` | Host local ISO timestamp added after `read_all()` returns |

Sources: [controller schema](../Control/temperature_control.py#L199), [logger record/write](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L79).

The supplied channel configuration enables K-type `probe_1` through `probe_5` (channels 0–4) and disables probes 6–8. A disabled probe is absent, not a zero-temperature measurement. An enabled probe whose read fails can be absent from `temperatures_c` and present in `errors`. The usual physical locations are now described in [the hardware map](02-hardware-and-connections.md#thermocouple-channels); sensor labels in a data file still require the actual run's placement record before that map is assumed. [Sources: channel configuration](../Config/temperature_config.py#L12), [per-channel read handling](../Control/temperature_control.py#L210).

If the whole logger iteration raises an exception, an error record has `logger_timestamp`, `logger_status="error"`, and `error`; it need not have normal temperatures or output-state keys. The logger continues attempting reads. The requested interval is 1 s, but sleep happens after reading/writing, so actual spacing includes operation time. The latest record supplied to sweep snapshots can also come from a relay wrapper's `read_all()` and may lack `logger_timestamp`. [Sources: logger loop](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L79), [relay wrappers](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L106).

Output states are software variables updated after output commands. They do not prove lamp light output, actual freezer compressor operation, physical contactor state, or camera boot completion. [Source: output methods](../Control/temperature_control.py#L108).

## Sweep summary schema

`sweep_summary.json` records:

| Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run_timestamp`, `sweep_name`, `sweep_index` | Host-generated name/time and numbered attempt; failed attempts can leave gaps among usable sweeps |
| `trigger_reason` | `time_interval`, `temperature_target_final`, or `temperature_safety_timeout_final` in the long runner; callers may supply another string |
| `camera_ip`, `remote_run_dir`, `local_run_dir` | Acquisition endpoint and original paths, which may become stale after data is moved |
| `status`, `error` | Capture/sweep-stage result; see transfer caveat below |
| `sweep_started_at`, `sweep_finished_at`, `sweep_duration_s` | Sweep-stage wall-clock endpoints and monotonic duration; transfer is timed separately |
| `transfer_started_at`, `transfer_finished_at`, `transfer_duration_s` | Added after successful copy, filename verification, and remote removal |
| `temperature_before_sweep`, `temperature_after_sweep` | Latest external logger/controller records around the sweep; the long runner fills the after-record after transfer |
| `homing`, `final_position` | Homing configuration/result and return-to-zero position when the successful path reaches those steps |
| `lamp` | Whether callbacks control it, warm-up duration, on/off flags |
| `filters` | Ordered list of successfully captured filters with position/exposure/path information |
| `camera_internal_temperature_readings` | Normally `before_capture` and `after_capture` read wrappers, including failure/disabled status if applicable |
| `camera_keepalive_stream_events` | Sweep-level stop/restart diagnostics |

Sources: [initial fields](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L224), [homing/lamp/filter fields](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L263), [timing and transfer fields](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L364), [after-sweep update](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L835).

Each `filters` entry includes `filter_number`, `target_position`, `actual_position`, `exposure_time_absolute`, `remote_image_path`, and `remote_metadata_path`. The entry is appended only after that filter's remote capture call returns. Controller position is a motor-control coordinate, not an independently measured optical wavelength or alignment result. [Source: filter entry](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L314).

**Interpretation caveat:** the sweep-stage status becomes `success` before transfer. Copy, filename verification, or remote removal can later fail, while this summary remains successful and lacks transfer timing. Test-level event/counts may report failure in that case. Check both levels plus actual files. `verify_local_sweep()` establishes file existence only; it does not compare hashes, parse JSON, or decode PNGs. [Sources: transfer ordering](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L364), [filename check](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L179).

## Image format and sidecar schema

The supplied camera settings request 1296 × 1032, `GRAY8`, 24 frames/s, gain 0. The pipeline encodes a single camera buffer as PNG. The image is therefore a requested 8-bit grayscale acquisition product; do not describe it as a higher-bit-depth raw sensor dump. The hardware/driver's physical exposure units and radiometric response still need confirmation. [Sources: configuration](../Camera_scripts/camera_config.py#L2), [capture pipeline](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L106).

Per-image JSON includes:

- Identity/storage: `timestamp`, `image_file`, `image_path`, `metadata_file`, `camera_device`.
- Requested image description: `width`, `height`, `pixel_format`, `image_encoding`, `actual_size_bytes`, `capture_status`.
- Requested controls: `requested_frame_rate`, `requested_exposure_time_absolute`, `requested_gain`.
- Readbacks as **strings**, retaining the `v4l2-ctl` output: `stream_parameters_before_capture`, `stream_parameters_after_capture`, `applied_exposure_before_capture`, `applied_exposure_after_capture`, `applied_gain_before_capture`, `applied_gain_after_capture`.
- Pipeline provenance: `gst_command` as argument list.
- Remote-entry additions: `capture_type="remote_trigger"`, `requested_exposure_from_cli`.

Sources: [sidecar object](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L148), [remote-entry metadata](../Camera_scripts/capture_remote.py#L36).

The camera validates successful pipeline exit plus image existence/nonzero size before writing the sidecar. It does not decode the PNG to verify actual dimensions or image content. A failure after image creation can leave a PNG without its JSON sidecar. The image timestamp is recorded immediately before launching the capture pipeline; it is not a hardware exposure timestamp or an exact timestamp shared by every filter in a sweep. [Source: capture and metadata ordering](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L126).

## Internal camera temperature schema

The sweep-level wrapper stores `label`, `host_timestamp`, `enabled`, and `status`, plus `stream_refresh_requested` when applicable. `status` may be `disabled`, `failed` with error text, or `success` with a `remote_payload`. Host wrapper success means the returned JSON was parsed, not that every internal sensor is valid. [Source: read wrapper](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L81).

`remote_payload` includes `timestamp`, `epoch`, `device`, `sensors`, and `errors`. Sources are the camera computer's `sensors -j` output and the V4L2 `sensor_temperature` control. lm-sensors entries contain chip/adapter/label/temperature and assigned friendly name. Names such as CPU, FPGA, or Sensor PCB are driver-based labels, not a verified wiring inventory. Preserve raw sensor keys to disambiguate them. [Sources: payload](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L335), [friendly mapping](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L20), [lm-sensors parsing](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L66).

The special `camera:sensor_temperature` entry contains `temp_c`, `name="Camera Sensor"`, `control_active`, and `stream_refresh` diagnostics. Code interprets its integer control as millidegrees, divides by 1000, and rounds to one decimal place. `control_active` reads the `temperature_control` control as a boolean when available. Exactly 20.0 °C adds `warning="exactly_20c_possible_default_or_stale_value"`; this is a possible-stale flag, not proof that every 20 °C observation is wrong. [Source: sensor conversion and warning](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L297).

These internal readings bracket a sweep and are not a continuous internal temperature log. External probe logging continues separately throughout pre-cool and measurement. Different sensor series should be aligned using their own timestamps and physical meaning rather than assuming identical sampling times.

## Timestamp conventions and alignment limits

| Timestamp/duration | Clock and meaning |
|---|---|
| Test/sweep folder timestamp | Acquisition-host `datetime.now()`, second precision, format `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS` |
| Most host JSON timestamps | Acquisition-host local `datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")`; no explicit UTC offset |
| Image sidecar `timestamp` | Camera-computer local time immediately before GStreamer pipeline launch |
| Internal `host_timestamp` | Host time at the start of the internal-temperature wrapper |
| Internal payload `timestamp` / `epoch` | Camera computer's local ISO conversion / Unix seconds; recorded after its sensor collection |
| Durations such as `sweep_duration_s`, `transfer_duration_s`, pre-cool duration | Host `time.monotonic()` elapsed time, generally rounded to 0.001 s |
| Deadline scheduling | Host wall-clock datetimes, checked by the run loop |

Sources: [host helper](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L59), [root names](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L429), [sweep time/duration](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L214), [transfer time](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L390), [camera image time](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L126), [internal timestamp](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L355).

No host/camera clock synchronization check or time-zone identifier is written by these acquisition functions. Clock agreement must be confirmed before assigning precise cross-device timing. Do not silently attach the documentation computer's time zone to historical acquisition timestamps. A sweep filename timestamp labels the start of the sweep; sequential filter images can be acquired later. `temperature_after_sweep` is filled after file transfer, while `sweep_finished_at` is set before transfer and before wheel shutdown completes. [Sources: acquisition ordering](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L376), [after-sweep snapshot](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L835).

## Metadata repair and legacy folders

Two separate repair scripts exist; their grouping conventions differ:

| Script | Group convention and writes |
|---|---|
| `repair_repeat_group_metadata.py` | Infers groups by base name/timestamp/consecutive repeat index; uses `<base>_<anchor_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>` as group ID; writes repeat group/index/count/base into test metadata and summary |
| `repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py` | Infers similar groups, reads camera ID from metadata/summary, uses `<camera_id>_<YYYY-MM-DD>`; updates metadata/summary and can rename root folders to camera-based names |

Sources: [older grouping](../Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py#L89), [older writes](../Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py#L137), [newer camera ID/grouping](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L108), [newer update and rename](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L164).

Both offer `--dry-run`. These reference commands inspect proposed changes and were not executed against result folders:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py "/path/to/results/root" --dry-run
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py "/path/to/results/root" --dry-run --rename-folders
```

The scripts infer membership; they do not recover missing experimental intent. A missing repeat index can split a sequence. They identify folders by `test_summary.json` existence rather than enforcing completed status, and their JSON loader returns an empty object for unreadable/invalid JSON. Review proposals and retain originals before any applied repair. The rename helper checks target-name collisions, but is not a general metadata migration: it updates selected top-level fields, not every nested sweep/event/image path. It instructs users to rerun analysis afterward to refresh CSV paths. [Sources: folder detection/load](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L52), [index grouping](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L140), [selected writes](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L164), [collision checks](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L220), [rerun notice](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L269).
