Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## What the analysis measures

The analysis follows features in camera images while recording the temperatures associated with each acquisition sweep. A sweep contains images from the configured filter positions. The current filter-to-analysis mapping is:

| Filter position | Analysis name | Filter identity | Processing | Nominal wavelength | Configured optical filter FWHM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `no_filter` | Open position | Spatial edge and signal statistics | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| 2 | `bp_780` | Thorlabs [FBH780-3](https://www.thorlabs.com/item/FBH780-3) | Spectral line profile | 780 nm | 3 nm |
| 3 | `bp_1064` | Thorlabs [FLH1064-3](https://www.thorlabs.com/item/FLH1064-3) | Spectral line profile | 1064 nm | 3 nm |
| 4 | `bp_1550` | Thorlabs [FBH1550-4](https://www.thorlabs.com/item/FBH1550-4) | Spectral line profile and background-region statistics | 1550 nm | 4 nm |

The owner confirmed the filter part identities on 27 October 2026, including **FLH1064-3** for the 1064 nm position. The narrow bands were chosen as discrete samples across much of the owner-described 400–1700 nm camera range. They do not provide continuous coverage or verify performance between the sampled wavelengths. The test is used with variants of the **qtec Hypervision** camera family rather than one fixed reference camera. [Owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

The wavelength and FWHM numbers above are the analysis configuration's nominal values; no measured transmission curve is used by the code. Filter bandwidth in nm is metadata; the implemented measured widths and movements are in image pixels. The analysis does not convert pixel widths to wavelength resolution, remove the finite optical filter bandwidth, or establish a physical distance per pixel. For component descriptions and supplier specifications, see [hardware and connections](02-hardware-and-connections.md#filterwheel-filters-and-position-calibration). [Filter mapping](../Config/analysis_config.py#L12), [analysis dispatch and metadata](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L776).

The primary quantities are spectral FWHM, spectral line position, spatial line spread function (LSF) Gaussian FWHM, spatial edge position, no-filter signal level, and dark-region level and spatial variation. Width describes the observed feature's sharpness; position tracks its movement. A change in these observables does not by itself identify which mechanical, optical, illumination, or sensor effect caused it.

The target is white **PTFE**, selected by the owner for its reflectance over the approximately 400–1700 nm range. A black 3D-printed cage over the PTFE produces the sharp dark lines used as spatial features. A halogen tube and silver-coated parabolic reflector focus illumination onto the target. These are owner-confirmed construction and selection details; no measured reflectance curve, calibrated Lambertian response, or quantified target-edge quality has been supplied. The analysis does not divide by a calibrated white reference or remove the target's edge response from the measured spatial width. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

## Image coordinates and current regions of interest

Images are loaded through Pillow into floating-point arrays. The analysis expects a two-dimensional intensity image and crops with `image[y0:y1, x0:x1]`. Coordinates are zero based; `x1` and `y1` are excluded. X is treated as the spatial direction and Y as the spectral direction. Intensity is reported as digital numbers (DN), meaning the stored image values; the scripts do not establish their conversion to electrons or radiometric units. [Image load and crop](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L43), [coordinate convention](../Config/analysis_config.py#L37), [DN plot labels](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L1136).

| Region | X interval | Y interval | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `central_dark_line_auto_right_edge` | `[450, 640)` | `[460, 500)` | Spatial edge profile in the no-filter image |
| `bp_780 / roi_1` | `[620, 650)` | `[245, 440)` | Spectral line at central spatial sample |
| `bp_780 / roi_2` | `[450, 480)` | `[245, 440)` | Spectral line at another spatial sample |
| `bp_780 / roi_3` | `[760, 790)` | `[245, 440)` | Spectral line at another spatial sample |
| `bp_1064 / roi_1` | `[620, 650)` | `[450, 640)` | Spectral line |
| `bp_1064 / roi_2` | `[450, 480)` | `[450, 640)` | Spectral line |
| `bp_1064 / roi_3` | `[760, 790)` | `[450, 640)` | Spectral line |
| `bp_1550 / roi_1` | `[620, 650)` | `[790, 995)` | Spectral line |
| `bp_1550 / roi_2` | `[450, 480)` | `[790, 995)` | Spectral line |
| `bp_1550 / roi_3` | `[760, 790)` | `[790, 995)` | Spectral line |
| `signal_1` | `[600, 670)` | `[460, 540)` | Signal statistics in the no-filter image |
| `signal_2` | `[600, 670)` | `[540, 620)` | Signal statistics in the no-filter image |
| `noise_1` | `[200, 680)` | `[460, 540)` | Background statistics in the 1550 nm filtered image |
| `noise_2` | `[200, 680)` | `[540, 620)` | Background statistics in the 1550 nm filtered image |

Source: [spatial region](../Config/analysis_config.py#L41), [spectral regions](../Config/analysis_config.py#L79), [signal and noise regions](../Config/analysis_config.py#L98). These coordinates describe the supplied configuration, not a permanent alignment standard. Verify them on images after changes to camera framing, optical alignment, or sensor format. The crop helper does not validate boundaries; NumPy may silently truncate an out-of-bounds crop.

Check that the fixed spatial ROI crosses the intended cage-produced dark line against the white PTFE in the current framing. Also check that the signal regions sample the intended illuminated target areas and that the spectral and background regions remain suitable. Knowing the target construction does not establish that these fixed pixel coordinates select the intended features on every camera or after a focus/alignment change. [Target description and usual setup](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

The owner verifies the wheel positions before every long test and adjusts manual focus when the camera is changed. Record those setup checks with the run and inspect the analysis regions after a camera change. Focus or framing changes can affect width and position comparisons even when the analysis code is unchanged. The offline analyzer does not verify that these manual checks occurred. Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Processing before measurement
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Processing before measurement

The loaded images are used directly. There is no dark-frame subtraction, flat-field correction, exposure normalization, image registration, saturation rejection, bad-pixel mask, or calibrated wavelength transformation in `analyze_sweep`. Background-region statistics are measured separately and are not subtracted from the spectral or signal images. [Per-filter processing](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L783).

For profile-based FWHM, centroid, and quadratic peak estimation, the common baseline correction is:

```text
b = 10th percentile of the one-dimensional profile p
q[i] = max(p[i] - b, 0)
```

The baseline is a percentile within that profile, rather than an independently acquired background. The spatial Gaussian fit instead fits its own constant offset to a local window of the raw absolute LSF. [Baseline correction](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L71), [Gaussian initialization](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L268).

The smoothing helper is a moving average with edge-value padding. Windows greater than one must be odd. The supplied configuration enables smoothing but sets both windows to `1`, which means no smoothing. Spectral smoothing, when increased, changes the profile used for spectral metrics. Spatial smoothing changes debug plot profiles only: the primary spatial Gaussian fit and raw diagnostics continue to use the unsmoothed gradient. [Smoothing helper](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L51), [spectral use](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L479), [spatial use](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L540), [current settings](../Config/analysis_config.py#L110).

Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Spectral profile, width, and position

For each spectral ROI, the script averages over X to obtain an intensity profile along Y:

```text
p[y] = mean of I[y, x] over the ROI's X pixels
```

Each filter has three independent profiles at different X locations. Each profile is measured before the resulting metrics are averaged across ROIs. The script does not average all three image strips into one common profile. [Spectral profile and measurements](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L470), [ROI aggregation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L794).

title: Freezer test analysis methodology
text:
Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Spectral FWHM
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Spectral FWHM

After the profile's percentile baseline correction, the largest sample defines the main peak. The algorithm walks left and right from this peak until it passes below half the peak height. At each side it linearly interpolates the crossing:

```text
h = max(q) / 2
crossing = i0 + (h - q[i0]) / (q[i1] - q[i0])
FWHM = right_crossing - left_crossing       [px]
```

It measures the connected peak near the maximum, rather than the distance between arbitrary above-half-maximum points across the entire ROI. It returns `NaN` for a nonpositive corrected peak, equal-valued crossing samples, or when the crossing search reaches either endpoint. In particular, reaching the first or last sample is rejected even if those two endpoint-adjacent samples could otherwise bracket a crossing. [FWHM implementation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L83).

The output is `bp_780_fwhm_px_mean`, `bp_1064_fwhm_px_mean`, or `bp_1550_fwhm_px_mean` after ROI aggregation. The bandwidth labels 3, 3, and 4 nm do not mean the measured pixel FWHM has been corrected for filter width.

title: Freezer test analysis methodology
text:
Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Spectral line position
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Spectral line position

The primary position is a local quadratic peak estimate. The algorithm baseline-corrects the profile, finds its maximum, and fits `a*x^2 + b*x + c` to at most five samples centered on the maximum. The peak estimate is `-b/(2*a)`. It falls back to the integer maximum if there are fewer than three samples, fitting fails, the parabola does not open downward, or its vertex lies outside the fit interval. The ROI's `y0` is added to obtain a full-image Y coordinate. [Quadratic estimator](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L169), [full-image outputs](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L497).

`peak_fit_y_px` therefore means a quadratic peak fit, not a Gaussian spectral fit. Positive Y shift means movement toward larger image row numbers. The code also records the integer peak, profile maximum intensity, ROI mean intensity, and a windowed centroid as diagnostics.

The quadratic estimator has no minimum signal-amplitude or contrast acceptance threshold. A weak or flat profile can still yield a finite integer fallback position even when its width is missing. Position validity therefore needs a profile/signal check, rather than a finite-number check alone.

The centroid is calculated from the baseline-corrected profile around the main peak, with a 20% peak threshold:

```text
centroid = sum(i * q[i]) / sum(q[i])        [px]
```

The summation uses indices strictly between the left and right search boundaries. This is a windowed main-peak centroid, rather than a full-ROI center of mass; endpoint handling can also exclude an endpoint sample. [Centroid implementation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L132).

Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Spatial edge width and position
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Spatial edge width and position

The no-filter spatial ROI crosses a dark vertical line. Averaging the ROI over Y gives an edge spread profile across X. The code computes a numerical gradient and its magnitude:

```text
ESF[x] = mean of I[y, x] over the ROI's Y pixels
signed_LSF = numpy.gradient(ESF)
LSF = abs(signed_LSF)
```

The differentiation sample spacing is one pixel. The implementation is a direct profile gradient; it does not perform slanted-edge oversampling or calculate an MTF curve. [Spatial profile construction](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L538).

title: Freezer test analysis methodology
text:
Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Selecting the intended edge
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Selecting the intended edge

Current `dark_line_auto` settings first find the ESF minimum inside the ROI near full-image `x = 560`, with search half-width 80 pixels. The code then searches 4–35 pixels to the right of that minimum for the largest positive gradient: the intended dark-to-bright edge on the bar's right side. The search bounds are clipped to the available ROI. These settings reduce the chance of switching to another bar or the opposite edge, but the detected minimum is simply the minimum ESF sample, not a fitted bar center. [Current edge settings](../Config/analysis_config.py#L41), [dark-line search](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L354).

The alternative `fixed_target` mode searches around `target_x` and `search_half_width`; left-edge and negative-polarity searches are also supported. If the requested polarity has no positive candidate, the algorithm tries the absolute gradient. If the search is still empty or zero, it falls back to the strongest absolute gradient across the entire profile. A returned fit is therefore not proof that the intended physical edge was selected. [Alternate mode and fallbacks](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L404).

title: Freezer test analysis methodology
text:
Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Gaussian LSF fit
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Gaussian LSF fit

The primary spatial measurement fits a Gaussian plus constant offset to the raw absolute LSF around the selected edge:

```text
g(x) = offset + amplitude * exp(-0.5 * ((x - center) / sigma)^2)
spatial_FWHM = 2.354820045 * abs(sigma)       [px]
edge_position = ROI.x0 + center             [px]
```

The supplied fit half-window is 5, giving at most 11 samples. The fit requires SciPy and at least five samples. Its initial offset is the local 10th percentile, amplitude is the local maximum minus that offset, initial center is the selected gradient maximum, and initial sigma is `max(1, half_window/3)`. Bounds constrain amplitude to nonnegative values, center to the fit interval, and sigma between 0.2 and `max(3*half_window, 1)` pixels. Offset is unbounded. [Fit model and checks](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L207), [initialization and bounds](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L268), [current fit settings](../Config/analysis_config.py#L117).

The fit returns `NaN` width and position if disabled, SciPy is unavailable, the profile/window is too short, amplitude is nonpositive, or fitting raises an error. The primary CSV fields are `no_filter_lsf_gaussian_fwhm_px_mean` and the derived spatial position shift. `gaussian_fit_success` records successful numerical fitting; it does not include a residual test, confidence interval, goodness-of-fit threshold, or physical edge validation. The fit covariance returned by SciPy is discarded. [Fit return values](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L302), [spatial metrics and diagnostics](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L594).

Additional spatial diagnostics include the raw absolute LSF FWHM, raw quadratic peak, windowed centroid, mean image intensity, selected edge position, search bounds, detected dark-line position, and `edge_contrast = percentile95(ESF) - percentile5(ESF)` in DN. The raw FWHM, quadratic peak, and centroid search the strongest peak in the whole absolute LSF. They can describe a different edge from the selected edge used for the Gaussian fit; disagreement is not automatically a fit error. [Diagnostic calculations](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L594).

text:
Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Signal and background-region measurements
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Signal and background-region measurements

The no-filter signal ROIs each produce mean, median, population standard deviation, 5th/95th percentiles, minimum, and maximum of all their pixels. The primary signal field, `no_filter_signal_signal_mean_mean`, is the unweighted mean of the two ROI means. It retains background offsets and is not exposure normalized. The field `no_filter_signal_signal_std_mean` is the mean of the within-ROI pixel standard deviations; it is not the uncertainty of the mean signal. [Signal statistics](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L517), [aggregation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L839).

The two noise ROIs are measured in the `bp_1550` image, away from the configured 1550 nm line location. For each cropped ROI with N pixels and mean mu:

```text
dark_mean = mean(I)                                      [DN]
noise_std = sqrt(sum((I - mu)^2) / N)                    [DN]
noise_rms = sqrt(mean((I - mean(I))^2))                  [DN]
```

`noise_std` and `noise_rms` are mathematically equivalent here: both are mean-subtracted population scatter across pixels. The script also records median, percentiles, minimum, and maximum. Primary outputs include `dark_noise_dark_mean_mean`, `dark_noise_noise_std_mean`, and `dark_noise_noise_std_std`. [Background calculation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L642), [filter selection](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L812).

These measurements can contain fixed-pattern variation, gradients, hot pixels, stray light, and other spatial structure. They are not temporal noise from a stack of repeated frames, independently measured read noise, dark-current rate, an SNR calculation, or confirmation that the shutter/light source was off. Whether the regions are physically dark under the intended setup remains an experimental validation item.

The owner previously reported condensation on bandpass filters together with reduced signal and blurred spatial information. Treat filter condition as a measurement-validity check when interpreting signal and width changes; these effects cannot automatically be attributed to the camera under test. This is an owner-reported setup concern, not an individual-result conclusion. Humidity sensing, purge, and filter heating have not been confirmed as installed. [Recovered freezer and wiring context](08-project-context.md#freezer-and-wiring-context).

Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Meaning of output suffixes

`average_metric_dicts` treats each ROI as one equally weighted measurement. For each numeric metric it writes:

| Suffix | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `_mean` | `numpy.nanmean` across ROI metric values |
| `_std` | `numpy.nanstd` across ROI metric values, population convention (`ddof=0`) |
| `_n` | Number of non-NaN ROI metric values |

Missing values are omitted from these summaries. Text diagnostics are skipped; booleans become 0 or 1, so a mean fit-success field is a fraction of ROIs whose fit succeeded. The CSV holds aggregated diagnostics rather than a full table of separate per-ROI metric records. [Aggregation implementation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L663).

The spectral standard deviation describes differences across the three X sample locations; it is not fit uncertainty or repeated-measurement uncertainty. There is currently one spatial edge ROI, so its aggregation standard deviation is zero whenever its metric is finite. Zero spread from one ROI does not establish zero measurement uncertainty.

Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md

### Within-test change

For each configured delta metric:

```text
metric_delta[sweep] = metric[sweep] - first_valid_metric_in_this_test
```

The baseline is selected independently for each column, so columns can use different baseline sweeps after missing measurements. The script processes lexically sorted `sweep_*` paths and does not explicitly sort the final rows by timestamp or numeric sweep index. The generated acquisition folder names must preserve chronological order for “first” to mean first in time. [Delta implementation](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L943), [sweep ordering](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L1311).

Configured deltas cover spectral FWHM, spectral quadratic peak position, spatial Gaussian edge position, and no-filter mean signal. Spatial Gaussian FWHM has an absolute output but is not included in the current `DELTA_COLUMNS`. [Metric lists](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L858).

text:
Document: Freezer test analysis methodology
Section: Temperatures
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

### Temperatures

`temp_<probe-name>_c` fields come from `sweep_summary.json / temperature_before_sweep / temperatures_c`. They represent the summary's pre-sweep reading; the analyzer does not average continuously logged temperatures over exposure time. It also calculates `temp_probe_2_minus_probe_1_c` and its absolute value when both columns exist. Those derived differences are in the diagnostic table, but are not in the explicit primary-field list. [Temperature parsing](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L702), [difference columns](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L929), [primary columns](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L888).

The owner's usual probe placement is:

| Field | Usual measured location | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `temp_probe_1_c` | Camera outer case on the side without the computer | Local exterior case temperature |
| `temp_probe_2_c` | Camera outer case on the computer side, described as the hotter side | Local exterior case temperature near the computer side |
| `temp_probe_3_c` | Camera side between the probe 1 and probe 2 locations | Another local exterior case temperature |
| `temp_probe_4_c` | Camera-facing upper surface of an aluminium tray in the upper freezer, away from the camera and lamp | Tray surface temperature |
| `temp_probe_5_c` | Underside of the same tray, away from heat sources | Tray underside temperature; usual pre-cool/endpoint control channel |

This is the owner-confirmed **usual map**, not an immutable channel assignment; record the placement used for each test. Under this map, `temp_probe_2_minus_probe_1_c` means computer-side exterior case temperature minus the opposite exterior case temperature. A positive value means the computer-side measurement is warmer. Its absolute-value field discards that direction. This is a difference between two surface readings, not a measured core-to-case gradient or a spatial gradient per unit distance. Probes 4 and 5 measure the tray surfaces; neither is a free-air probe or an internal camera/optics measurement. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

The test first cools with the freezer on and camera off, then measures with the freezer off and camera on. The owner describes the camera and intermittently operated lamp as heat sources during the subsequent warm-up to the endpoint. In the reviewed runner the lamp is switched on for sweep capture and off afterward, rather than held on throughout measurement. Treat the data as a transient warming history: local case, tray, and internal temperatures can differ and lag each other. Matching two samples by probe 5 alone does not prove equal camera-core or optical temperatures. The code does not impose a steady-temperature hold, a controlled heating ramp, or a correction for thermal lag. [Owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [pre-cool sequencing](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330), [camera startup](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L559), [sweep lamp control](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L301).

Camera-internal readings, if recorded in the sweep summary, are flattened as `camera_internal_<reading-label>_<sensor-name>_c`. Status and error fields are retained in diagnostics. All available camera-internal temperature columns ending `_c` are added to the primary table. Missing camera temperatures are not reconstructed from another source. [Internal-temperature parsing](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L725), [primary table inclusion](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L960).

Section: Repeat-cycle comparison
Source: knowledge_base/06-analysis-methodology.md
Status: owner review in progress; version 0.3; compiled 2026-10-29

## Repeat-cycle comparison

The owner's purposes include statistical repeatability comparisons between camera units and comparisons during camera development. Within-unit repeated thermal cycles and differences between units or revisions are separate comparison questions. Identify the actual camera unit and revision for every test; the family name qtec Hypervision alone is insufficient. For repeatability estimates, compare physically comparable units and setup conditions. For an intentional development comparison, record the changed design and keep other conditions comparable. Individual outcomes remain outside this setup knowledge base. [Owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

`analyze_repeat_tests.py` compares absolute positions, not within-test deltas. For each `repeat_group_id`, `sweep_index`, and available position metric, it chooses the first nonmissing row sorted by `repeat_index` and then `test_folder`, and subtracts that value from each cycle:

```text
repeat_delta_px[cycle, sweep] = absolute_position[cycle, sweep]
                             - earliest_valid_cycle_position[sweep]
```

The four quantities are the three spectral quadratic peak positions and spatial Gaussian edge position. If cycle 1 is missing or invalid for a metric, a later valid cycle becomes that metric's reference. Both comparison viewers apply this calculation to the tests currently loaded, so excluding the original reference cycle changes the plotted baseline. [Batch repeat calculation](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L208), [original viewer calculation](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit.py#L536), [updated viewer calculation](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L622).

This aligns cycles by sweep index only. It does not interpolate onto equal temperature, elapsed time, heating/cooling branch, or thermal-equilibrium conditions; it does not register the images. Comparison at the same sweep index is therefore only a matched-condition comparison if the actual acquisition protocols and temperature histories support that interpretation.

The current repeat script produces within-group position differences, and the viewers can overlay different units' metrics. They do not automatically pool units into a statistical population, separate variation within units from variation between units, correct camera-to-camera focus/alignment differences, or calculate a validated inter-unit repeatability statistic. The population definition, comparable setup conditions, and statistical treatment still need to be specified for that use. Record unit identity, hardware/design revision, manual focus adjustment, wheel verification, exposure/gain, ROI configuration, actual probe-placement map, and the thermal protocol when preparing such a comparison.

Current repeat-group inference normalizes group identity to `camera_id + YYYY-MM-DD`, preferring `repeat_group_start_date`, then a date extracted from an existing group ID, then a folder timestamp, then test date. Two genuinely separate sequences from the same camera on the same date can consequently be merged. Missing an explicit shared start date can split a multi-day sequence into daily groups. [Batch group inference](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L120), [updated viewer group inference](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L162).

The batch “cycle start” table selects the minimum sweep index across the entire combined dataset, then keeps rows at that index. It does not select the first available row separately for every cycle. Both combined CSV filenames currently receive the same combined table; `position_repeatability_by_sweep.csv` is not a separate statistical summary. [Cycle start selection](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L238), [CSV writing](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L344).

## Review items before treating the method as validated

1. Verify that each ROI selects the intended PTFE/cage feature or spectral/background region in the current framing and remains valid through the expected image movement.
2. Confirm the rationale and validation for the spatial sample locations and percentile/fit settings; filter identities and the narrow-band sampling rationale are owner-confirmed above.
3. Establish whether the noise ROIs are free of relevant signal and whether spatial scatter is the intended noise observable.
4. Define the exposure policy and whether signal comparisons require normalization.
5. Specify wavelength/spatial calibration, uncertainty estimation, saturation checks, fit-quality criteria, and acceptance limits if those are required for reporting.
6. Define matched thermal states and treatment of case/tray/optics temperature differences and lag, the unit/revision population and statistical treatment for between-unit comparisons, and how independently started same-day sequences should be identified.

These are gaps in documented experimental validation, not proposed changes already implemented in the scripts. Operational commands, output names, and known viewer issues are documented in [Analysis tools and troubleshooting](07-analysis-tools-and-troubleshooting.md).

## Recommended analysis workflow

1. Retain a record of the operator's wheel-position verification before every long test and manual focus adjustment when changing cameras. These are owner-confirmed setup practices; the analysis tools do not enforce them. [Owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).
2. Inspect the region overlays on an early and late sweep, after a camera change, and on any substantially shifted image. Confirm that the spatial ROI crosses the intended black cage line against the white PTFE and that signal, spectral, and background ROIs remain appropriate. Check that `Config/analysis_config.py` matches the current framing and metric settings. [Target description](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).
3. Analyze an individual test and inspect `sweep_diagnostics.csv` for errors, missing filters, ROI counts, and fit success.
4. When comparing repeat cycles, regenerate stale analyses with the same settings, check unit/revision, probe-placement and repeat-group metadata, then run repeat analysis or load the desired cycles in the updated viewer. Keep within-unit cycle repeatability distinct from comparisons between units or development revisions.

Keep the acquisition images and metadata alongside their derived analysis. Record the code revision and configuration used for reporting; the analyzer does not save a configuration snapshot or version stamp into its output itself. See [Analysis methodology](06-analysis-methodology.md) for definitions and interpretation limits.

## Preview the configured regions

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/preview_analysis_rois.py "/path/to/sweep_folder"
```

Input is one sweep folder containing `sweep_summary.json` and the image files named by the basenames of its `remote_image_path` entries. The tool draws the configured regions and saves:

```text
<sweep_folder>/analysis_roi_preview/
    filter_1_no_filter_roi_preview.png
    filter_2_bp_780_roi_preview.png
    filter_3_bp_1064_roi_preview.png
    filter_4_bp_1550_roi_preview.png
```

## Analyze one test folder

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py "/path/to/test_folder"
```

The analyzer scans sorted `sweep_*` paths, reads each sweep summary, and processes the images named there. It identifies a local image as `<sweep_folder>/<basename of remote_image_path>`; the remote directory itself is not required. An unknown filter number is skipped. A missing configured image records `filter_<number>_missing = True`. An exception during a sweep records a row with `sweep_name` and `analysis_error`; the script can still print “Analysis complete” after individual sweep failures. [Sweep input parsing](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L752), [error handling](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L1311).

Outputs:

| File or folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `analysis/sweep_metrics.csv` | Selected primary metrics and available camera-internal temperature columns |
| `analysis/sweep_diagnostics.csv` | All aggregated numeric metrics, positions, ROI spreads/counts, exposure values, temperatures, derived differences, missing-filter flags, and sweep errors |
| `analysis/plots/` | Available metric plots listed below |
| `analysis/profile_debug/` | Profile plots when `DEBUG_PROFILE_PLOTS = True` |

The command overwrites both CSV files and removes the existing `analysis/plots` directory before rebuilding plots. A successful exit confirms that processing reached the end; inspect diagnostics to determine which measurements succeeded. ## Analyze repeat cycles

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py "/path/to/results_root"
```

The root can be an individual test or a parent tree. Test discovery requires `test_summary.json` and at least one `sweep_*` path. It recursively discovers test summaries unless the root already qualifies as one test. Existing `analysis/sweep_diagnostics.csv` files are reused; it runs the single-test analyzer only when that file is absent. Use `--force` when settings or source code changed and existing analyses need regeneration:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py "/path/to/results_root" --force
```

The child analyzer is addressed relative to the current directory, so run this command from the repository root. `--force` invokes the single-test analyzer and therefore overwrites its derived CSV/plot outputs. If a child analyzer exits unsuccessfully, its `check=True` subprocess call stops the batch before the later per-table loading error handler can skip it. [Discovery](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L73), [reuse and subprocess](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L166), [main processing loop](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L307).

Output is written under `<results_root>/repeat_analysis/`:

```text
combined_sweep_diagnostics.csv
position_repeatability_by_sweep.csv
cycle_start_position_repeatability.csv
cycle_start_spectral_position_delta.png
cycle_start_spatial_position_delta.png
```

The first two CSV files currently contain the same combined table. The cycle-start table and plots are based on the global minimum sweep index, which can exclude cycles missing that index. These tools compare absolute sensor positions at matching sweep indices; consult the methodology page before calling the result thermal return accuracy. [Cycle-start table](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L238), [plot outputs](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L253), [CSV outputs](../Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py#L344).

## Interactive comparison: two supplied versions

Both viewers read existing `analysis/sweep_metrics.csv` files, optionally merge absolute position columns from adjacent `sweep_diagnostics.csv`, add test metadata, calculate repeat deltas, and provide Plotly overlays and a selected-data CSV download. They do not analyze images or regenerate missing measurements. They offer overview, spectral resolution, spectral shift, spatial performance, signal stability, camera internal temperatures, cycle repeatability, and custom plot tabs. [Original loading](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit.py#L125), [updated loading](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L543), [updated tabs](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L1329).

The rig tests variants of the qtec Hypervision camera family, so use `camera_id` to identify the individual unit rather than putting only the common family name in that field. Record the hardware/design revision and relevant setup differences in `notes` or accompanying run metadata. Include the focus adjustment after a camera change, wheel-position check, exposure/gain, ROI settings, actual probe-placement map, and thermal protocol when comparing tests. The usual probe map is documented in [analysis methodology](06-analysis-methodology.md#temperatures); it can change between tests. The metadata editor exposes camera ID, date, duration, operator, and notes; it does not provide structured fields or automatic comparability checks for all these details. The updated editor preserves additional fields already present. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026), [updated metadata editor](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L893).

For statistical repeatability between units, select physically comparable units and revisions under comparable conditions. When evaluating a deliberate development change, label that revision difference and avoid treating it as unexplained unit variation. Do not combine different units into one repeat group to make the within-group return-error calculation act as an inter-unit statistic: the viewers provide overlays and within-group reference differences, not a population-level repeatability model. The experimental comparison plan must define that statistical treatment. Individual performance outcomes belong in the separate camera-development knowledge base.

| Aspect | `compare_tests_streamlit.py` | `compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browsing | Builds a JSON metadata catalog, then automatically loads selected tests' CSVs | Browses JSON metadata first; CSVs load after **Load checked data** |
| Selection | Individual-test or repeat-group multiselect | Checkable individual-test or repeat-group browser, explicit load/clear controls |
| Summary backfill | Limited date/duration fallback | Also backfills camera ID, repeat fields, and additional date sources |
| Metadata save | Replaces the file with five editor fields, dropping other fields | Preserves existing fields, including repeat identity, then updates editor fields |
| Cache refresh after edit | Clears metrics and file-discovery caches | Also clears summary and metadata caches |

Source: [original initial catalog](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit.py#L678), [original editor](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit.py#L633), [updated metadata fallback](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L249), [updated editor](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L953), [explicit loading](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L1225).

### Reading viewer plots correctly

The viewer drops rows missing any selected plotting fields and sorts lines by the chosen X variable. A temperature X axis therefore sorts by temperature rather than acquisition order; a heating/cooling loop may be drawn in a misleading order. Missing points are removed before plotting, so `connectgaps=False` does not by itself preserve every gap in the original measurement sequence. No interpolation, image registration, or fitted temperature-response model is applied. [Updated plot preparation](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L684), [line plotting](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L711).

Choose a temperature axis using the map recorded for that test. In the usual arrangement, probes 1–3 are camera-case surface readings and probes 4–5 are opposite surfaces of an aluminium tray away from the camera/lamp; probe 5 is not a free-air or camera-core temperature. The measurement stage is a transient warm-up with the freezer off, camera on, and lamp switched during sweeps. Keep the native sweep order and temperature histories available when interpreting gradients or lag; the viewer does not compensate for them or establish thermal equilibrium. [Temperature interpretation](06-analysis-methodology.md#temperatures), [owner review R2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r2-owner-review-and-component-photos-29-october-2026).

Repeat references are recalculated from the loaded selection. To compare with cycle 1, include its valid data and verify group identity. Both viewers index discovered tests by folder basename, so duplicate folder names under different parent directories can overwrite each other in the selection dictionary. [Updated test dictionary](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L1161), [repeat calculation](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L622).

## Metadata repair tools

These tools change existing result metadata and can optionally rename folders. They infer groups from folder names; they do not recover the original experimental intent from measurements. Inspect a dry run and back up the affected metadata before applying a repair. No repair was performed while building this knowledge base.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py "/path/to/results_root" --dry-run
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py "/path/to/results_root" --dry-run
PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py "/path/to/results_root" --dry-run --rename-folders
```

`repair_repeat_group_metadata.py` groups names matching `<base>_repeat_<index>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>`, sorting by base and timestamp. It starts a new group at index 1, a base-name change, or a gap/nonconsecutive repeat index. It writes a timestamp-anchored `<base>_<timestamp>` group ID, index, count of discovered members, and base to both `test_metadata.json` and `test_summary.json`. It does not write `repeat_group_start_date`. [Grouping](../Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py#L89), [written fields](../Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py#L137).

`repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py` uses the same general grouping rule but sets camera/date-based identity, `repeat_group_start_date`, camera ID, repeat index/count, and summary root path. With `--rename-folders`, it renames to `<camera_id>_repeat_<index padded to 3 digits>_<timestamp>`. It checks destination collisions within each group, writes metadata first, then renames. Removing `--dry-run` applies the requested changes. Re-run analysis after renaming to refresh recorded paths. [Grouping](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L125), [metadata fields](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L164), [rename handling](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L192).

Both repair scripts treat malformed or unreadable JSON as an empty dictionary. An applying run can consequently replace unreadable original metadata with only reconstructed fields. Count is the number of discovered group members, not necessarily the originally planned repeat count. Camera/date-based IDs can collide for separate same-camera sequences starting the same day. These are reasons to review the dry-run grouping against the acquisition records before applying it. [First JSON loader](../Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py#L34), [second JSON loader](../Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py#L52).

## Troubleshooting reference

| Symptom | What to inspect |
| --- | --- |
| No tests appear in the viewer | Correct results root; presence of `analysis/sweep_metrics.csv`; cached discovery; duplicate folder basenames |
| A sweep is absent from plots | `analysis_error` in diagnostics; missing images; nonfinite metric; missing chosen X/Y values |
| Spatial Gaussian width or shift is missing | SciPy availability; fit enabled; ROI alignment; valid edge and enough fit samples |
| Spatial position suddenly jumps | Wrong dark-line minimum/edge; fallback to another gradient peak; changed framing; inspect debug profiles and selection diagnostics |
| Width or position differs after changing cameras | Check recorded unit/revision, manual focus adjustment, alignment, ROI placement, and wheel-position verification before attributing the difference to unit behavior |
| Raw spatial position differs from Gaussian position | Raw diagnostics can follow the strongest edge in the whole ROI while the Gaussian uses the selected target edge |
| Spectral FWHM is missing | Peak/crossings too close to an ROI boundary; feature clipped; weak/flat profile; wrong ROI |
| Spectral widths change after smoothing edits | Spectral smoothing changes the measurement input; compare analyses using identical settings |
| Spatial metrics do not change after smoothing edits | Spatial smoothing is used for debug display only |
| Signal changes between filters/runs | Check exposure, illumination, background, ROI placement, camera settings, and temperature; no exposure correction is applied |
| Signal changes when the target or lamp setup changes | Check PTFE/cage framing, halogen/reflector alignment, focus, and saturation; the analysis does not perform calibrated white-reference normalization |
| Signal loss or blurring at lower temperature | Inspect bandpass filters for condensation, an owner-reported setup concern; separate optical-path effects from camera behavior |
| “Noise” seems high or disagrees with another tool | This metric is spatial population scatter in the 1550 nm image, rather than temporal/read noise |
| Repeat cycles split over several days | Inspect `repeat_group_start_date` and group inference; folder-date fallback can split a sequence |
| Separate sequences merge | Camera/date identity may collide; verify grouping before interpreting repeat deltas |
| Repeat baseline changes after selection | The viewer recomputes the reference from loaded tests; include the intended baseline cycle |
| Metrics differ at the same displayed probe temperature | Confirm the actual probe map, warming history, camera-case/tray differences, lamp timing, and thermal lag; matching the usual tray-mounted probe 5 does not establish equal optical/core temperatures |
| Values remain unchanged after reanalysis | Cached viewer tables or repeat analyzer's reuse of existing diagnostics; clear/restart viewer and use `--force` when appropriate |

### Plot error-bar limitation in the current analyzer

The general error-bar helper chooses an error column by replacing **every** `_mean` substring with `_std`. For ordinary FWHM names this selects the intended ROI spread. For `no_filter_signal_signal_mean_mean`, it selects `no_filter_signal_signal_std_std`: the spread between within-ROI standard deviations, rather than `no_filter_signal_signal_mean_std`, the spread between mean signals. For `dark_noise_dark_mean_mean`, it asks for `dark_noise_dark_std_std`, which is not generated, so the dark-level plot falls back to a line without error bars. [Error-column selection](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L1004), [available signal metrics](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L517), [available dark metrics](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L642).

Use the explicit CSV definitions for interpretation until this plotting behavior is reviewed. ROI spread is not a confidence interval or a validated uncertainty budget, and the single configured spatial ROI produces zero aggregation spread by construction.

The owner confirms that the apparatus tests variants in the **Qtec Hypervision camera family**, with no single fixed reference camera. The test has two purposes: assess repeatability across units of the same type, and evaluate the effects of changes. The camera family is an owner-supplied identification; it is not evidence that the reviewed scripts use a manufacturer SDK. Current capture code uses V4L2 and GStreamer. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [capture pipeline](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L114).

Normal pre-cool uses **`probe_5` at 5 °C**. The 12 °C value in the preserved local configuration was intentionally used for a shorter recent trial. Operators verify/calibrate filter positions before every run because the internal motor reference may drift, and manually focus on the target plane whenever the camera changes. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [operating preparation](04-running-the-test.md#operator-preparation).

An earlier camera warm-start workaround was abandoned after the owner traced the startup problem to faulty camera hardware, which was unacceptable. The owner confirms the thermal sequence: freezer cooling with camera off, then freezer off before camera startup. The camera and sweep-switched lamp warm the chamber toward its endpoint; camera/freezer operation does not overlap normally. Removing camera power directly is the accepted routine shutdown practice. The usual map is exterior-shell probes 1–3 and opposite tray-surface probes 4–5, with changes allowed per test. | ID | Question / gap | Current limit |

| C01 | What are the acceptance criteria for position, width, signal, and noise? | No pass/fail thresholds are implemented |
| C02 | What is the intended definition of spectral resolution, and is there a wavelength calibration? | Present FWHM is in pixels and includes the bandpass-filter line shape |
| C03 | Confirm image orientation, ROI locations, the chosen dark-bar edge, and acceptable movement before ROI retuning | ROIs are fixed image coordinates, not image registration |
| C04 | Confirm physical units of `exposure_time_absolute`, camera processing, gain, and effective output bit depth | Stored format is GRAY8; exposure normalization is not performed |
| C05 | Are background ROIs optically dark at all temperatures? Is temporal noise or true dark-current analysis required? | Current noise metric is spatial DN scatter in a filtered image |
| C06 | How should saturated, clipped, dim, condensed, partial, or misaligned images be excluded? | Existing computations do not establish a complete image-quality acceptance policy |
| C07 | Should filter bandwidth be deconvolved, or should results remain observed profile widths? | Code does not deconvolve filter bandwidth |
| C08 | What uncertainty should be reported: fit uncertainty, spatial ROI variation, temporal repeatability, or all three? | Current ROI standard deviations are not general measurement uncertainty |
| C09 | How should case/tray gradients and thermal lag be handled in comparisons? | Usual locations are known; transient measurements do not directly establish optical-core equilibrium |
| C10 | Should comparison interpolate on temperature/time, compare only matched conditions, or show native samples? | Existing comparison tools are exploratory; they do not create a validated matching methodology |
| C11 | How should repeat groups remain unique across multiple sequences on the same day? | Default group ID uses camera ID and date; folder repair tools can modify metadata |
| C12 | How should inter-unit reproducibility be quantified, and which comparisons control unit/revision/focus differences? | The test purpose is confirmed; current within-group delta plots do not themselves produce a population-level statistical study |

- **Usual probe map, changeable by test:** probe 1 non-computer outer shell; 2 computer/hot outer shell; 3 side between those shell locations; 4 camera-facing/top face of the upper aluminium tray; 5 underside of that tray. - **Thermal sequence:** cool with freezer on and camera off; switch freezer off at the cold threshold; then start the camera. Camera and lamp heat warm the chamber toward the endpoint. Normal operation does not power camera and freezer together. The code confirms that the lamp is sweep-switched rather than continuously on.
- **Power and shutdown:** the owner accepts direct camera power removal as normal practice. A 5 V supply feeds MCC, Tic, network switch and Hall sensor. Two 24 V supplies separate lamp inrush from the other power arrangement after lamp startup briefly interrupted the camera. The exact XDR/NDR load assignment still needs its wiring map; the freezer appliance is rated 230 V, so low-voltage control and mains power are distinguished.
- **Local AI:** GitHub knowledge-base access through a deploy SSH key is already working according to the owner. No credential is included here; index freshness/answer quality was not independently tested.

| A single text/Markdown document | `exports/FreezerTest_Knowledge_Base.md` | Self-contained prose with source paths retained; the application may split it into smaller passages |
| A JSONL document loader | `exports/documents.jsonl` | One record per canonical document; read `text` as content and preserve metadata |
| A pre-chunked JSONL pipeline | `exports/chunks.jsonl` | Each record has `id`, `document_id`, `source_path`, `section`, `text`, `kb_version`, and content digest |

The pre-chunked export splits at section boundaries and limits chunk size; a long section may be split into continuation chunks with its document/section heading repeated. Chunking is a starting point, not a tuned retrieval configuration. The downstream system must still embed/index these records and retrieve them at answer time. Table and code-block continuations may need neighboring chunks.

Keep the source manifest and `reference/` files available as evidence, but do not index the historical configuration snapshot, CAD meshes, build scripts, ZIP files, caches, raw temperature log, or duplicate export formats as current operating instructions. Canonical chapters summarize accepted hardware/CAD facts. If you index source code separately, label it with the reviewed revision and distinguish it from the human documentation.

## Recommended answer instruction

The following instruction can be adapted to the local AI's knowledge or retrieval settings:

> Answer FreezerTest questions from the retrieved knowledge-base passages and cite their document/section. Version 0.3 includes owner reviews through 29 October 2026; the older acquisition-source snapshot does not prove deployed-file identity. Distinguish usual setup, actual per-run settings, code behavior, photographed labels, and unknowns. Normal pre-cool is 5 °C on probe_5, usually on the tray underside; the old 12 °C profile was a shorter trial. Usual probes 1–3 measure the exterior case and 4–5 opposite tray surfaces; placements may change by test. The freezer cools with camera off, then switches off before camera startup; camera and intermittent lamp heat warm the chamber. Direct camera power removal is the owner's accepted normal shutdown. The target is white PTFE with a black printed cage, illuminated by a reflected halogen tube; it is not established as a calibrated reflectance standard. Cameras are Hypervision variants, not one fixed reference build. Do not invent missing facts, individual results, or permissions to operate equipment.

For an AI with equipment-control tools, answering an operational question does not itself authorize executing the command. This corpus includes hardware-active command examples, especially preflight, calibration, diagnostics, and the runner. Indexing documentation should not trigger them.

## Retrieval checks after import

Use these as manual checks. The expected answers summarize the reviewed snapshot and must change if that snapshot is superseded.

| Question | Expected answer / evidence |
|---|---|
| What happens during one complete repeat? | Freezer on/camera-lamp off for pre-cool, freezer off and settle, camera boot/keepalive, sweeps while camera and intermittent lamp heat warm the chamber, endpoint or limits, power-cut cleanup; document 04 |
| What is the normal pre-cool threshold, and why does the old configuration say 12 °C? | Normally probe_5 ≤5 °C; 12 °C was a deliberate shorter trial; documents 01, 03, 04 |
| What is the reference camera model? | Qtec Hypervision variants are tested; record the unit/revision rather than assume a single fixed reference build; documents 01, 02, 08 |
| Do the repeat plots establish statistical reproducibility across camera units? | That is a test purpose, but existing plots calculate within-group deltas/overlays; a defined inter-unit statistical model and controlled revision/setup records are still needed; documents 06, 09 |
| What must be checked when preparing a run or switching cameras? | Verify wheel positions before every long test; manually set focus to the target plane after a camera change; document 04 |
| What does `probe_5` measure physically? | Usually the underside of the upper aluminium tray, away from camera/lamp; not free air or camera core. Check the actual test's map; documents 02, 05 |
| Where are the other usual probes? | 1 non-computer outer shell, 2 computer/hot outer shell, 3 side between them, 4 top/camera-facing tray surface; placements may change; document 02 |
| Are camera and freezer on together, and is the lamp continuously on? | No overlap in normal operation. The lamp is on for sweep captures and off between sweeps; documents 03, 04 |
| What forms the image target? | White PTFE plus a black 3D-printed cage, illuminated by a halogen tube and silver-coated parabolic reflector; no calibrated reflectance/target-transfer function is supplied; documents 02, 06 |
| How is the camera normally shut down? | By removing power, accepted by the owner as routine practice; documents 03, 04 |
| Is 120 seconds the exact image-to-image cadence? | No; configured wait is scheduled after a sweep, so capture and transfer take additional time; document 04 |
| Which filters and exposure settings are configured? | No filter, Thorlabs FBH780-3, FLH1064-3, FBH1550-4; historical exposure control values 3000, 15000, 8000, 15000; confirm per run; documents 01–03 |
| What units are the spectral width and shift in? | Pixels; no wavelength calibration or filter deconvolution is implemented; document 06 |
| Is the reported noise the camera's read noise? | No; spatial DN scatter from configured ROIs in a bp_1550 image; document 06 |
| Where do captures live before and after transfer? | Camera staging under `/root/scripts/data`; permanent host path from local configuration; failed sweeps may remain remotely; document 05 |
| Is preflight safe to run during acquisition? | No; it can operate real outputs through controller connection/disconnection; documents 04, 07 |
| Does the generic product documentation establish every tested unit's detector/optics/revision? | No; family documentation is context, while unit-specific configuration requires its own record; documents 02, 08, 09 |
| Is a dry-air purge installed? | Not confirmed; it was suggested historically; document 08 |
| Which camera performed best? | Individual results are excluded; this corpus cannot answer; README and document 01 |

An adequate first import should retrieve the relevant passage, preserve the implementation/intent distinction, and admit unknowns. A fluent answer without source support is not a successful check.

## Updating and sharing

Use the Markdown pages as the editable master and regenerate exports after review. Replace outdated indexed versions rather than accumulating contradictory drafts. The portable ZIP includes canonical documents, exports, source manifest, reference evidence, CAD files, component photographs and previews; it excludes acquisition results and acquisition source code. Human-readable labels/meanings are transcribed into the chapters so the AI can retrieve them without reading the photos. The historical configuration snapshot is not imported by the scripts. Keep the source repository alongside the knowledge base for clickable code references.

The existing deploy key is a credential of the AI's connection, not knowledge-base content. No private key or token is included in the corpus. Repository access follows the repository's permissions. A successful fetch and correct answers using the latest version are separate checks; the access is owner-confirmed, while current retrieval/index freshness still needs to be checked in that AI.

# Glossary

Status: terminology for version 0.3

| Term | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| Bandpass filter | Optical filter passing a limited wavelength band; configured at 780, 1064, and 1550 nm. Nominal bandwidth is not the measured instrument width |
| Capture | One camera image and its sidecar metadata at one filter position |
| Centroid | Intensity-weighted profile coordinate; distinct from the raw peak location or a fitted center |
| DAQ | Data-acquisition device; the network MCC unit reads thermocouples and handles digital input/output |
| DIO | Digital input/output; individual bits control lamp, camera power, and freezer, and read the Hall sensor |
| DN | Digital number, an image's numerical intensity value; not automatically photons, electrons, radiance, or normalized signal |
| DRTB-2 | Omega DIN-rail thermocouple terminal-block family used inside the freezer; exact fitted type suffix remains to be recorded |
| Edge position | Coordinate of the selected spatial transition; selection depends on ROI and edge-search mode |
| ESF | Edge-spread function, a profile across an image edge |
| Filter position | Wheel slot number mapped to a configured motor coordinate; not necessarily degrees or full motor steps |
| FWHM | Full width at half maximum. Spectral and spatial widths in the present pipeline are image-pixel widths |
| GRAY8 | Configured 8-bit grayscale capture format; not evidence of the detector's native ADC precision |
| Hall sensor | Magnetic reference input used to home the filter wheel; configured active-low |
| Homing | Searching for a Hall edge, approaching it slowly, and setting the motor coordinate reference |
| Keepalive stream | Continuous discarded-frame camera stream between sweeps; paused for still capture when configured |
| Local override | A setting imported from `Config/local_config.py` into system configuration, with effect only where code consumes it |
| LSF | Line-spread function; spatial analysis derives an edge-gradient profile and fits a Gaussian locally for its main width metric |
| MCC / uldaq | Measurement Computing device ecosystem and the Python-facing Universal Library interface used in this project |
| Offner | The optical architecture named by the owner; the detailed prescription is not supplied |
| PNG sidecar | JSON metadata file accompanying a captured PNG image |
| Pre-cool | Freezer-on stage before measurement; reaching the configured probe threshold completes it, while timeout aborts the test |
| Probe | Named external temperature channel. Usual probes 1–3 measure the exterior camera shell; 4 and 5 measure opposite aluminium-tray surfaces. The actual map may change per test |
| PTFE/cage target | White PTFE backing with a black 3D-printed cage forming dark image lines; not established as a calibrated reflectance or edge-transfer standard |
| Repeat | One complete test within an automated sequence, normally with its own test directory |
| Repeat group | Identifier used to associate repeat tests; current default is camera ID plus date |
| ROI | Region of interest; configured rectangular image crop, using x for columns/spatial direction and y for rows/spectral direction |
| SCP / SSH | File-transfer and remote-command tools linking host and camera |
| Spatial noise | Within-image variation of pixel DN in an ROI; differs from variation over repeated frames at the same pixel |
| Sweep | Sequential captures at all configured filter positions, plus metadata and transfer |
| TEC | Thermoelectric cooler; references to it do not establish a particular mode, setpoint, or control implementation in this repository |
| Tic / ticcmd | Stepper controller and command-line interface used to move the filter wheel |
| V4L2 | Linux video/control interface used by the camera scripts |

Metric-specific definitions and formulas are in [analysis methodology](06-analysis-methodology.md); filenames and field definitions are in [data and metadata](05-data-and-metadata.md).
